It has been revealed that neurons expressing tdTomato were imaged on a Nikon AXR confocal microscope equipped with a ×60/1.40 numerical aperture oil-immersion objective, controlled by NIS-Elements software (Nikon). Excitation lasers were 488 nm, 561 nm and 640 nm and the same gain and power settings were used across all conditions for each culture. Then 2,048 × 2,048 images (pixel size 0.111 µm) were taken as sequential linescans, generating a z-stack with steps of 0.3 µm to cover the depth of the tdTomato-positive neuron. For one culture, 1,024 × 1,024 images were taken (pixel size 0.222 µm). Several z-stacks were taken to cover the entire dendritic arbour of each cell. The investigator was blinded to the treatment condition for synapse density imaging. Images were then analysed in Fiji (ImageJ) using custom-written macros. First, maximum projections of the tdTomato channel were used to trace dendrites using the NeuronJ plugin. Binary traces were dilated three times to generate a dendritic mask. Maximum projection images of the Synapsin1 (presynaptic) staining were filtered with a top hat filter of radius of two and an automated threshold using the Moments algorithm was applied, followed by watershed processing to separate merged puncta. Particles of size 0.08–2.5 µm2 were analysed to generate presynaptic ROIs. Maximum projections of the Homer1 (postsynaptic) staining were filtered using a top hat filter of radius 1 and underwent automated thresholding using the Renyi Entropy algorithm, followed by watershed processing and analysis of particles of size 0.00–1.2 µm2 to identify postsynaptic ROIs. Postsynaptic ROIs were enlarged by 1 pixel and analysed for overlap with both the dendrite masks and presynaptic ROIs. Synapses on dendrites that consisted of both a presynaptic and postsynaptic partner were counted and divided by the total area of the dendrite mask to calculate the synapse density for each cell.

Around 10,000 HaloTDP iNeurons were plated on 5,000 primary rat astrocytes in 96-well imaging phenoplates (Revvity) and matured in synaptic media (BrainPhys, StemCell Technologies), with 1× N2-Max Supplement (R&D Systems), 1× N21-Max Supplement (R&D Systems), 10 ng ml−1 NT3 (StemCell Technologies), 20 ng ml−1 GDNF and BDNF (Peprotech), 2.5% FBS (Thermo Fisher Scientific), 1× Non-Essential Amino Acids (Thermo Fisher Scientific), 0.2 mg ml−1 cAMP (Sigma-Aldrich), 1× GlutaMAX (Thermo Fisher Scientific), 1% penicillin–streptomycin (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and 200 nM ascorbic acid (Sigma-Aldrich)54. HaloPROTAC (30 nM) was added at DIV14. Plates were longitudinally imaged and neuronal cell bodies automatically quantified by means of phase-contrast detection using the Incucyte S3 imaging platform. Subsequently, plates were fixed with PFA at weekly timepoints and stained for NeuN and DAPI (as above). NeuN automated imaging was carried out on an Opera Phenix high-content screening system (Revvity) and NeuN/DAPI counts quantified using Harmony v.4.9 Software.

According to recent reports, mouse C57BL/6J embryonic stem cells (B6.N6) were transfected with a targeting vector, designed to replace mouse intron 20 with the orthologous human sequence using an 817-bp 5′ homology arm and a 1,462-bp 3′ homology arm. Two risk allele SNPs for ALS and frontotemporal dementia (rs12973192 (G) and rs12608932 (C)) were present within the human intron sequence used to replace the endogenous mouse intron. Two CRISPR–Cas9 site-specific nucleases targeting the boundaries of intron 20 (5′-GGAGCCAGCTGTATGCGTCT-3′ and 5′-GTACCAAGGAGACGTGGCAT-3′) were cotransfected as pX459 (Addgene no. 62988) vectors. Following transient selection in 1.8 μg ml−1 puromycin for 48 h, applied 24 h after transfection, clones were grown, isolated and screened for homologous recombination events using primers 5′-LR-FWD1–REV1 and 3′-LR-FWD1–REV1 to amplify over the 5′ and 3′ homology arms, respectively. qPCR assays were designed against the mouse and human intron 20 and used to verify the loss of the mouse intronic sequence and the gain of the human intronic sequence. Recombinant embryonic stem cells were microinjected into albino C57BL/6J blastocysts and the resulting chimeras were bred with C57BL/6J mice. The offspring were genotyped for the presence of the targeted allele.

An aberrantly targeted line of mice was generated in which the homologous recombination event had occurred, but with a tandem duplication of the vector that led to a portion of the vector backbone being integrated within intron 23. Despite the tandem duplication, the human intron was correctly positioned within the context of the murine Unc13a gene, which was expressed and appropriately spliced. We refer to this mouse line as a human UNC13A reporter mouse and it was used in subsequent in vivo studies.

Sources indicate that mice were injected with an recombinant AAV (rAAV) (PHP.eB) that expresses a synthetic microRNA targeting the mouse Tardbp gene (PackGene BioTech; gift from Trace Neuroscience) along with UNC13A ASO (M21-4) or vehicle at 8 weeks of age (P56-62). rAAV-Tardbp-microRNA was diluted in sterile PBS and administered as a 150-µl tail-vein injection. A total dose of 1.4 × 1012 vg was delivered per mouse. Mice were subsequently exposed to 5% isoflurane for anaesthetic induction, before reducing the concentration to 1.5–2% for maintenance purposes. Analgesia was provided with 5 mg kg−1 oral Metacam administered in a custard carrier 60 min before surgery, followed by subcutaneous injections of 10 mg kg−1 meloxicam and 0.1 mg kg−1 buprenorphine. A subcutaneous injection of 2 mg kg−1 bupivacaine was given as an incisional block shortly after anaesthetization. Intracerebroventricular injections of 10 µl of ASO (30 mg ml−1 in artificial cerebrospinal fluid (ACSF) (Harvard Apparatus, 59-7316) supplemented with extra Mg2+ to achieve a 3:1 Mg2+:ASO ratio) or vehicle (0 mg ml−1 in ACSF + Mg2+) were performed using a Hamilton syringe at a rate of 1 µl min−1. Injection coordinates were set at −0.35 mm y, +1 mm x, −1.75 mm z relative to the line of best-fit bregma and brain surface. The incision was subsequently sutured closed, and animals were returned to their home cages. Mice were closely monitored for 3 days post-surgery and provided with 5 mg kg−1 Metacam in custard carrier every 24 h postsurgery for the duration. Injections were performed blinded to treatment group. Mice of both sexes were included, with n = 9 (6 females, 3 males) for ASO and n = 7 (5 females, 2 males) for ACSF vehicle. Three weeks post-injection (P77-83), thoracic spinal cord was dissected and snap-frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at −80 °C. Sample size for the in vivo mouse experiment was based on a pilot study showing a large effect of TDP-43 knockdown in one humanized UNC13A mouse. Subsequently, all animals that could be generated during the experimental period were used. When injections spanned many days, equal numbers of mice from each group were injected on each day. Injections were not randomized.

Sources indicate that spinal cord samples were immersed in 0.5 ml of ice-cold QIAzol Lysis Reagent (Qiagen, 79306) in 2-ml tubes (Fisher 15545809). Two 1.4-mm ceramic beads (Omni International 19-645) were added to each tube and samples were homogenized at 4 °C using a Precellys 24 touch homogenizer (Bertin Technologies) at 6,500 r.p.m. for 30 s on, then 120 s off, four times. Samples were centrifuged for 5 min at 12,000g at room temperature and supernatants were transferred (400 μl) to new tubes. Chloroform (100 μl) was added to each sample and then samples were vigorously shaken for 15 s followed by incubation at room temperature for 3 min. Samples were centrifuged at 12,000g for 15 min at 4 °C and then the upper aqueous phase was transferred to new tubes (200 µl). Then 70% ethanol (200 μl) was added and samples were mixed by vortexing. RNA was purified from samples using the RNeasy (Qiagen) kit including the on-column DNase (Qiagen) digestion step. RNA was eluted with water and quantified using a NanoDrop (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Reverse transcription was performed as described above using the RevertAid first-strand cDNA synthesis kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific). For RT–qPCR the following reagents were used: Mouse Tardbp (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Mm01257504_g1) and Mouse Hprt1 (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Mm03024075_m1), custom UNC13A cryptic exon assay. For RT–PCR, Mouse Unc13a exon 20 forward and Mouse Unc13a exon 21 reverse primer were used (Supplementary Table 4).

Recent findings suggest that datasets were assessed for normality. For normally distributed data, t-tests were used for statistical comparison of two groups. One-way ANOVA tests with post-hoc multiple pairwise comparison of means was used for statistical analysis of three or more groups. For non-normally distributed data, non-parametric tests were used. For MEA analysis, log2[fold change] is presented in figures as a matter of clarity, but all analyses were performed on raw data, or on fold changes derived from raw data for rescue experiments, using paired ratio t-tests. Statistical tests were carried out using GraphPad Prism (v.10.6.1; GraphPad Software) or with the R statistical library. Sample size and P values are specified in figure legends.

In a recent development, statistical analyses of pooled datasets from several experiments (electrophysiology and synaptic imaging) were performed in R (v.4.4.1) using the lme4 (ref. 72) and lmerTest73 packages. Data were log1p-normalized before fitting a Gaussian linear mixed-effects model (LMM) by restricted maximum likelihood with experimental batch as a random intercept to account for between-batch variability. The intraclass correlation coefficient for batch ranged from 0 to 0.4451 across datasets. Inclusion of batch as a random intercept was confirmed by a likelihood ratio test. Normality of model residuals was assessed by Shapiro–Wilk test and Q–Q plot inspection; W statistics ranged from 0.85 to 0.99 across datasets. For datasets in which residuals showed greater deviation from normality (W < 0.90), results were confirmed separately using a Gamma generalized LMM with log link (glmmTMB74), which yielded consistent conclusions in all cases, supporting the robustness of the primary LMM analysis. For experiments designed a priori to test cryptic exon deletion or ASO rescue of the TDP-43-knockdown phenotype, TDP-43 KD was set as the reference condition, with all comparisons made directly against this baseline. P values were derived from Satterthwaite degree-of-freedom-corrected t-tests. For experiments without a priori comparisons, Tukey’s test for multiple comparisons was used.

All iPS cell experiments used the established human iPS cell line WTC11 (GM25256), obtained from the NIGMS Human Genetic Cell Repository at the Coriell Institute for Medical Research. The line was originally derived from de-identified adult dermal fibroblast with informed consent and approval from the University of California, San Francisco Institutional Review Board. No new human tissue was collected; therefore, this work did not constitute human subjects research and did not require further ethics committee approval at University College London, King’s College London or Leibniz-FMP-Berlin. All procedures complied with relevant institutional guidelines for the use of human cell lines.

In a recent development, WT astrocytes were obtained from Wistar rat embryos (Charles River Laboratories) as described above. Animals were housed in individually ventilated cages with a 12-h light–12-h dark cycle, with ad libitum access to food and water. Facilities were maintained at 20–24 °C and 55 ± 10% relative humidity. Ethical review and approval was not required for this part of the study because only Schedule 1 procedures performed by a competent individual were used, which are exempt under the Animals (Scientific Procedures) Act 1986.

The mice were housed in individually ventilated cages with a 12-h light–12-h dark cycle, with ad libitum access to food and water. Facilities were maintained at 20–24 °C and 55 ± 10% relative humidity. All studies were conducted with ethical approval from the institutional Animal Welfare and Ethical Review Body and in accordance with the UK Home Office Animals (Scientific Procedures) Act 1986. Following Tardbp knockdown, mouse body weights were monitored daily, and mice were culled if body weight decreased by more than 15% from baseline. All mice that survived more than 2 weeks post-injection were included in the analysis.

WT astrocytes were obtained from male and female P0-P1 C57BL/6J mice (Charles River Laboratories). Adult mice were kept at the animal house of the Max Delbrück Center (Berlin Buch) under individual ventilated cage and specific pathogen-free conditions with food and water ad libitum, on a 12 h light–12 h dark cycle, at room temperature (22 ± 2 °C) and humidity levels of 55 ± 10%. All experiments performed in Berlin complied with European law and the state of Berlin animal welfare body (Landesamt für Gesundheit und Soziales; LAGeSo).

Recent findings suggest that a, Amplicon sequencing of PCR products from Fig. 1a indicates correct HaloTag editing of TARDBP. b, Manhattan plots of low pass whole genome sequencing results from parental and HaloTDP WTC11 iPSC lines indicate no large chromosomal rearrangements are present. c, PCR from genomic DNA at CRISPR–Cas12 off target loci (n = 1). d, IGV plot of sequencing results from PCR products in (c) indicates no edits are present at off-target sites. e, HaloTDP iNeurons were untreated (NT) or treated with the indicated concentration of HaloPROTAC for 4 days and processed for western blot analysis indicating a dose response curve of HaloPROTAC on TDP-43 knockdown. f, Quantification of western blots in (e) n = 3 biological replicates. g, HaloTDP iNeurons were untreated (NT) or treated with 30 nM HaloPROTAC for 3 h in the presence of DMSO, proteasome inhibitor MG132, or NEDD8 E1 inhibitor MLN4924 (n = 2). h, Immunofluorescence analysis of HaloTDP iNeurons at DIV28 with the indicated neuronal markers indicates neurons have a cortical (CTIP2 ISL1+) glutamatergic (NKX2.1−) deep layer (PAX6−) identity. i, RT-PCR analysis of WT and HaloTDP iNeurons demonstrates the HaloTag induces a mild loss of TDP-43 function and can induce cryptic exon inclusion in the indicated transcripts (n = 2). Graphs for (f) and (h) represent mean ± s.e.m. Uncropped gels are shown in Supplementary Fig. 4.

Sources indicate that a, RT-qPCR analysis of correctly spliced UNC13A at exon 20–21 junction n = 10 biological replicates from 3 experiments. b-f, Analysis of control and CRISPRi-mediated TDP-43 knockdown in DIV 28 iNeurons. (b) RT-PCR analysis of UNC13A splicing at exon junction 20–21 shows the inclusion of a long and short cryptic exon after TDP-43 KD. (c) Quantification of results in (b) n = 6 from 3 experiments. PSI (Percentage Spliced-In). (d) RT-qPCR analysis shows a reduction in correctly spliced UNC13A at exon 20–21 junction following TDP-43 KD n = 12 from 3 experiments. (e) Western blot analysis indicates a dramatic decrease in UNC13A protein after TDP-43 KD. (f) Quantification of results in (e) n = 7 from 3 experiments. g, RT-qPCR analysis of DIV38 HaloTDP iNeuron cultures indicates similar expression of glutamate receptors in untreated (NT) and TDP-43 knockdown conditions. A cryptic exon in CamK2B and cryptic polyadenylation in STMN2 result in reduction of mRNA transcripts. n = 8 from 2 experiments. h, Representative western blot analysis of control and CRISPRi-mediated UNC13A knockdown in iNeurons n = 3. Graphs in (a) (c) (d) (f) and (g) represent mean ± s.e.m. Statistics for (c) and (d), two-sided Student’s t-test. Statistics for (f), two-sided paired t-test on log-transformed, loading control normalized values. Statistics for (g), two-sided Student’s t-test with additional Bonferroni adjustment for multiple comparisons. * P < 0.05; ** P < 0.01; *** P < 0.001; **** P < 0.0001; ns (not significant). Uncropped gels are shown in Supplementary Fig. 5.

a, AMPAR blockade using CNQX abolishes mEPSC activity. b, mEPSC amplitude from control (n = 12) and UNC13A depleted (n = 13) iNeurons pooled from 3 experiments. c, mEPSC amplitude from control (n = 20) and TDP-43 knockdown (n = 22) HaloTDP iNeurons from 3 experiments. d, Quantification of passive membrane properties for UNC13A knockdown iNeurons. e, Quantification of passive membrane properties for TDP-43 knockdown iNeurons. f, Representative MEA raster plots following AMPAR blockade using CNQX. Quantification indicates CNQX treatment at DIV41 abolishes network synchrony on multi-electrode array recordings, with minimal effects on firing rate. 30 s shown. g, Quantification of additional MEA metrics following CNQX treatment, UNC13A knockdown and TDP-43 knockdown. Each dot represents a well in the CNQX plot, while in TDP-43 and UNC13A plots, each dot represents the area under the curve for a separate experiment. h, Phase contrast images showing cell coverage on multi-electrode array plates. Scale bar = 350 µm. Graphs for (b) (c) (d) and (e) represent mean ± s.e.m. Statistics are from a Gaussian LMM on log1p-transformed values with batch as a random intercept, p-values are from two-sided Satterthwaite-corrected t-tests. Statistics in (f), a two-sided paired ratio t-test. ** P < 0.01, * P < 0.05; ns (not significant).

In a recent development, a, PCR from genomic DNA of WT SH-SY5Y cells and CE Del SH-SY5Y cells indicated successful deletion of the genomic region of UNC13A containing the sequence corresponding to the exon 20–21 cryptic exon (n = 1). b, Amplicon sequencing of PCR products in (a). c–g, Analysis of control and TDP-43 KD in WT and CE Del SH-SY5Y cells. (c) RT-PCR analysis of UNC13A splicing indicates CE deletion rescues splicing at the UNC13A exon 20–21 junction after TDP-43 KD. (d) Quantification of results in (c) n = 8 biological replicates from 3 experiments. PSI (Percentage Spliced-In). (e) RT-qPCR analysis of TDP-43 and correctly spliced UNC13A reveals CE deletion rescues UNC13A RNA levels after TDP-43 KD. n = 8 biological replicates from 3 experiments. (f) Western blot analysis of protein lysates shows CE deletion rescues UNC13A protein levels after TDP-43 KD. (g) Quantification of results in (f) n = 5 biological replicates from 3 experiments. Graphs in (d) (e) and (g) represent mean ± s.e.m. Statistics for (d) and (e), one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple comparison test. Belgian journalist admits Sylla may be ‘more inclined’ to move to England: “His dream destination”

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan have been heavily interested in Massire Sylla recently, but it seems they may struggle to sign him, let alone in January.

It’s no secret that Milan want to sign a central defender and whilst Goncalo Inacio is the leading name, he’s not the only one in the mix. Instead, there are several public names of interest and Sylla is one of them.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

First linked by Matteo Moretto, his name has become more popular in reports linking the Rossoneri to defenders and he seems like a concrete target for the January mercato. Yet, it seems like it will be difficult to bring him to San Siro.

Speaking to MilanNews, Het Nieuwsblad journalist Tjorven Messiaen looked at Massire Sylla and what his future had in store.

In a recent development, in Italy, there’s been talk of AC Milan’s interest in Sylla. What’s being said about him in Belgium?

Recent findings suggest that “I saw that AC Milan have linked him with him. In Belgium, we discovered him through social media, and the USG hasn’t confirmed anything yet. It’s possible, however, that AC Milan has drawn attention to the boy, because he’s playing great football.

“His move to AC Milan is unlikely to materialise in January, however, as both Sylla and the club would be more inclined to listen to offers from the Premier League. He’s the kind of player who would be a perfect fit for the English league.”.

What are his main strengths and best qualities?

Sources indicate that “He’s young, he’s good in duels, he’s quick. He’s also very good at ball control. He’s a complete defender; he has the potential to become one of the best, and he’d be a perfect fit in the Premier League, which, among other things, is Sylla’s dream destination.”.

What aspects of his game still need improvement?

According to recent reports, “It’s hard to say, especially since his growth in recent months has been impressive. I’d say he needs to gain more experience, which will come simply by playing. So I don’t see many things he needs to improve to take the next step in his career.”.

Do you think Union Saint-Gilloise (USG) would be willing to let him leave in January, or do you think any transfer discussions will be postponed until the summer?

“I don’t think USG will let him leave in January. The only possible scenario, which I don’t think will happen, but which is the only solution anyway, is for USG to sign him in January but keep him at least until the end of the season, especially since the club never sells its best players in January.

“I also think interested clubs could spend a lot of money, but Union won’t let him leave in January.”.

Could you describe him in three adjectives?

“Quick, physical, and full of character, because he’s someone who always has problems when he has to make decisions.”.

Which defender would you compare him to?

“Considering his development, I’d say Pacho. He came from nowhere in Belgium, developed, moved to Frankfurt, and then ended up at PSG. In Sylla’s case, I think he’ll go straight to the Premier League. He has everything it takes to be perfect for this league.”.

He’s still very young. Do you think he’s ready to play for a big club in a big city like Milan?

“He’s still very young, but he’s humble, calm, and we mustn’t forget that he arrived last year, in January, from the Norwegian second division. He played very little last year, but he’s very strong mentally and has started this season as if he’s been playing with this team for years.

“I can’t imagine USG without Sylla today, especially since we’re talking about one of the best defenders in the league. At the end of the season, he’ll make a significant leap in his career, but in my opinion it won’t be AC ​​Milan because he’s waiting for the Premier League. And from what I know, several English clubs are already ready to make him a player.

“So AC Milan could give him a try, but it will require a major project and a lot of money.”.

In a recent development, we shall have to see how January develops and whether he could be sold on the project. However, it certainly doesn’t bode well from these comments.

Industry News: Lethal Trent Alexander-Arnold sends Tuchel a statement in England victory

📅 29 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6306 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.
  • England always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie.
  • TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

England always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the fresh half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24.

Will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

Having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the substantial delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

Sources indicate that “I make that run time and time again,” Gordon mentioned of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”.

A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

Recent findings suggest that as for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

Sources indicate that “Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel noted. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

Sources indicate that czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL.

England had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

Recent findings suggest that even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

Sources indicate that “I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold remarked later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”.

Two minutes after the break, Alexander-Arnold suddenly burst into life. He won the ball back in his own area and then drove forward in search of the return. When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon remarked, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”.

Recent findings suggest that kane scored the second just a minute before he was replaced and Bellingham took the captain’s armband and the role as a No 9. One day someone will have to step into those goalscorer’s boots on a permanent basis and try to replace Kane – although it may be a while yet.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

Recent findings suggest that “If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel noted when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against New Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

“I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

“But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”.

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

Trent Alexander-Arnold provided an assist for Anthony Gordon in the Real Madrid full-back’s first cap in 15 months. Gordon, meanwhile, has now scored in the first two Nations League games of the campaign and is staking his case to be an indispensable player for Tuchel.

“He’s getting there. He’s defending his shirt, he’s defending his position, an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain,” Tuchel stated.

“He was very decisive today and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult, but the technique and finishing was excellent. He scored against Spain, so he has decisive actions and he’s defending his shirt and his position. He does it on the highest level and he’s a very notable player.”.

England returned to winning ways with a 2-0 win over Czech Republic in Prague.

Pavel Sulc’s first-half red card after a VAR review of his clumsy challenge on Elliot Anderson took the sting out of the initially lively hosts and Anthony Gordon gave Thomas Tuchel’s men a deserved lead early in the second half.

The forward headed home a fantastic cross by Trent Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first start under the German coach, before skipper Harry Kane scored to settle any nerves.

Recent findings suggest that so who played well for England and who failed to impress? Rate each player with our voting tool, and have your say in the comments.

I thought we were very professional second half. We stepped up and needed to be more dynamic, bring more urgency into our play, which we did. We kept that intensity going and and the effort was till there. Deserved victory.

Industry observers note that strange to get an early red card. Not the best for the spectators, not the best for the team. It’s an awkward one. But we got the win.

According to recent reports, to guide it into the goal, there was an awful lot [for Anthony Gordon] to do. Good pass, good goal. Both full-backs were good. The position in the second half suited Trent more than the position in the first half. Lewis was excellent on the other side.

In a recent development, we have used all the outfield players after two matches so credit to all of them. Now it’s notable to relax and enjoy the evening, do a good recovery and prepare for Saturday.

Sources indicate that I think it was good. They go down to 10 men and it should be easier for us to win the game, But in fact it makes it more difficult. They get very compact and defend with a lot of players around the box and it’s hard to break them down.

We got that [goal] at the start of the second half which is what we needed. The longer it’s 0-0, it gets harder and harder and harder.

[Where do you place your assist?]  It’s up there for sure. I spoke to Ant at half-time and stated if I get into those half-spaces I’m looking to put it in so make sure you get to the back post. I didn’t expect it to work so swiftly.

He’s a willing runner, great to play with him. I saw the run and was able to execute the pass,.

In a recent development, it’s always a pleasure and an honour to represent my country. It’s been a long time. I’ve always believed that I can play for England and I want to. Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Championship data highlights exactly what West Ham’s midfield is still missing

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (584 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Claretandhugh

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fascinating piece of Championship analysis from Loft Insights on X may provide an uncomfortable reminder of where West Ham’s midfield falls short.
  • The graphic plots central midfielders based on two key metrics: line-breaking passes per 90 minutes and ball-winning actions per 90 minutes.
  • The most interesting takeaway for me was not necessarily which players stand out, but where West Ham’s own midfield profiles sit on the chart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fascinating piece of Championship analysis from Loft Insights on X may provide an uncomfortable reminder of where West Ham’s midfield falls short.

The graphic plots central midfielders based on two key metrics: line-breaking passes per 90 minutes and ball-winning actions per 90 minutes. Put simply, it measures which players are able to progress the ball through opposition lines while also contributing defensively.

The most interesting takeaway for me was not necessarily which players stand out, but where West Ham’s own midfield profiles sit on the chart.

It has been revealed that the Championship’s elite midfielders increasingly occupy the top-right quadrant, combining progression and defensive intensity. That is why the chart identifies Norwich City’s Kenny McLean as one of the Championship’s most complete midfielders, posting outstanding line-breaking numbers while maintaining strong defensive output, despite only featuring for ten games out of fifteen due to an ankle injury.

Meanwhile, Portsmouth’s Ebou Adams is highlighted as a “defensive monster”, producing exceptional ball-winning statistics while still offering significant progression. Sheffield United’s Kalvin Phillips (yes the same player that flopped on loan at West Ham!), Queens Park Rangers’ Jonathan Varane and Norwich’s Jacob Wright also occupy impressive positions, demonstrating the ability to impact both sides of the game.

Mohamadou Kanté is viewed as a dynamic ball-carrying midfielder with strong physical attributes, but his game is built more around energy and transition play than elite progression metrics. Arne Engels offers technical quality and creativity, yet is generally more comfortable operating higher up the pitch than acting as a defensive controller.

The data is only based on players who have played an average of 540 mins so one omission is Tomas Souček, whose strengths have always been obvious. The Czech international on paper would arguably be the Championships most effective midfield goalscorer (3 in 7 appearances so far) and I’d expect him to feature highly for aerial presence. However, if plotted on a graph measuring line-breaking passes and ball-winning volume, he would likely owe more to his physicality and attacking threat than his ability to dictate possession through midfield.

That perhaps explains why West Ham can sometimes appear disconnected between defence and attack.

Too often there is a reliance on direct balls into attacking areas rather than building through the centre of the pitch. Equally, when possession is lost, the midfield does not always possess the combination of mobility and defensive output needed to regain control quickly.

Industry observers note that west Ham arguably have midfielders who can create and win duels. What they appear to lack is a genuine “two-way” midfielder capable of consistently ranking highly in both categories.

That was precisely what Declan Rice offered during his time at the club. His ability to recover possession and immediately progress the ball remains incredibly difficult to replace.

The reality is Rice was never truly replaced, although finding a like-for-like successor was always going to be a near-impossible task.

According to recent reports, former West Ham midfielder James Ward-Prowse’s position on the chart is also interesting. A casualty of Nuno’s reign, he ranks among the highest players for line-breaking passes but has one of the lowest ball-winning outputs. Ward-Prowse excels at progressing possession but offers relatively little defensive contribution compared to the league’s most complete midfielders.

Above all the data serves as a reminder that Koppen’s recruitment and Parker’s existing choices for midfield should focus less on individual statistics and more on complete profiles.

Because the numbers suggest that is where Championship matches are increasingly won.

Industry observers note that arsenal transfer interest in Alphadjo Cisse is starting to take shape. Arsenal are monitoring the development of AC Milan starlet Alphadjo Cissé, although his sensational start to the season could prove to be costly for Mikel Arteta.

The 20-year-old has made a blistering start to his Serie A career and attracted interest from a number of Premier League clubs after his impressive displays so far. Arsenal are reported to be interested.

Published: 13:01 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 20:45 EST, 14 November 2026.

A former Premier League referee was mistakenly declared dead by football chiefs this week.

Sources indicate that on Tuesday, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) declared Keith Cooper had died aged 78. But he is alive and well.

The news reached the ears of the Wembley Cup final referee when he went out to his local sports centre for a flu jab only to be told: 'You were dead.'.

The Football Association of Wales posted a statement online and a tribute on social media to announce his death, but then withdrew it within an hour.

Mr Cooper, who is the father of former Nottingham Forest and Leicester boss Steve Cooper, told a Welsh sports website: 'I walked into the sports centre yesterday to have my jab and the fellow went, "You were dead!".

'Well, I'm not dead, I'm here and I'm OK!'.

The blunder appears to have emerged after the Wiltshire FA announced the death of another referee called Keith Cooper, who the football chiefs in Wales believed was the other Keith Cooper.

The FAW statement remarked: 'Keith was a well-known figure who enjoyed an exceptional career at both domestic and international level and would later hold the position of FAW Referees' Officer following his retirement in 1996.

On Tuesday, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) unveiled Keith Cooper had died aged 78.

Mark Beeney goalkeeper of Leeds United is Sent Off of by Referee Keith A Cooper for hand ball outside the area during the Premier League match between Manchester United and Leeds United at Old Trafford on April 17, 1996 in Manchester, England.

Former professional football John Fashanu is pictured with referee Keith Cooper during a Wimbledon F.C. match.

'Born and raised in Pontypridd, he is considered one of Wales' best match officials through his highly-regarded status in the game.

'In addition to his work with FAW, Keith was also a valued member of the Wiltshire FA Council who recognised his 'integrity, passion and commitment' in their tribute to his services to the game.

'Everyone at the FAW sends their condolences to his family and friends at this sad time.'.

Mr Cooper oversaw the 1994 League Cup final between Aston Villa and Manchester United, won by Villa 3-1, and worked in radio punditry after hanging up his whistle.

The FAW has not issued an explanation over the posted tribute. His family has not yet commented on the error.

But the unfortunate mistake has not spared the FAW from ridicule by other football fans.

One said: 'We always said there was only one Keith Cooper - turns out there are two.'.

Another remarked: 'Glad the whistle wasn't blown too early on Keith and much respect to the family of the other one.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal Women missed the chance to end their frustrating run of draws at home as London City Lionesses came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw at the Emirates Stadium.

Sources indicate that frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in an exciting start to the game. But Isobel Goodwin equalised almost straight away. Despite creating plenty of chances, Renée Slegers’ side failed to find a second goal.

Arsenal have now lost their last five WSL games at the Emirates. The results were yet another frustrating afternoon for the defending champions, who put in a strong display against Barcelona in Europe earlier in the week.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal started on a high note, creating some dangerous chances with their quick play. Emily Fox and Lisa Baum worked really well together down the right, and Ona Batlle had a great chance from the edge of the box.

As the pressure mounted, Fox surged forward and played a perfectly weighted through ball to Alessia Russo. The striker turned and played the ball back to Maanum, who rounded off her impressive comeback from injury by finishing.

Arsenal had little time to rejoice. London City equalised just a minute later as Goodwin found herself in space to fire past Misa Rodríguez.

The visitors looked more confident after equalising, but Mary Earps was proving a tough ask for Arsenal to score past. The ex-Manchester United shot-stopper kept out Baum and made some key stops from Arsenal’s efforts.

Rodriguez also had to make a key stop before half-time as she got a hand to Daniela Arques Lazaro’s powerful strike to keep the scores level.

The Gunners continued their attacking play but were made to work hard by a high pressing side from London City.

But Arsenal still managed to create some chances. Caitlin Foord put Earps under pressure and Maanum and Baum combined before the latter saw her curl just wide.

London City posed a threat too. With Kadidiatou Diani and Grace Geyoro causing defensive problems for Arsenal, Geyoro fired into the side netting.

Industry observers note that delphine Cascarino had the game’s defining moment of the second half, hitting the crossbar from outside the box. However, Arsenal were lucky to escape and Maanum came close to winning the game, hitting the woodwork from a dangerous counter.

Slegers brought on Kyra Cooney-Cross and Olivia Smith in the 72nd minute to provide some new energy. Smith looked lively upon entering the game, but Earps denied her efforts and Batlle’s cross.

Emily Fox had to be substituted due to injury in the final moments of the game, but Slegers later indicated that she would be okay.

Industry observers note that the Gunners were unable to find a winning goal and will now turn their attention to their Champions League clash on Thursday with Lyon. They will then face West Ham at home in the WSL.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, declan Rice’s new contract shows how much of an asset he is to Mikel Arteta. His recent performances show why.

Recent findings suggest that the England international has reportedly signed a new five-year deal which will keep him at the Emirates Stadium until 2031. The contract is a reward for the midfielder who has been instrumental in Arsenal’s success since he moved to the club in 2023 from West Ham.

Rice has not just provided the presence and protection that Arsenal were hoping for with their £105 million signing. He has continued to develop his game, especially after returning to his deeper midfield role this season.

Rice came in as a defensive midfielder, but Arteta swiftly saw how much he could offer higher up the park.

Recent findings suggest that his physicality, ability to run into the box and set piece threat made him a useful left-sided number eight. Rice had a huge impact in midfield for Arsenal, bringing goals and a fresh attacking threat.

But Rice has played in a more advanced position on the right-hand side of the midfield duo this season, and this has not limited his impact but instead highlighted another key part of his game.

Rice has made the most line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season, with Opta stats reported by Sky Sports showing he is second only to Premier League players.

This is of particular interest, as he has often come under criticism for his distribution. But he is averaging nearly double the amount of line-breaking passes he did last season.

While his running ability is still an asset, he is also becoming much better at penetrating through the defensive lines to find his teammates, giving Arsenal another option to move the ball forward with.

The development of Rice is key in securing a newly introduced contract at Arsenal.

The 27-year-old has already proven to be one of the most reliable members of Arteta’s squad and has shown great longevity by only missing five games out of his 119 Premier League outings in his first spell at the club.

Former West Ham teammate Jack Wilshere has also praised Rice’s strong work ethic, ability to adapt and natural leadership qualities.

In a recent development, the reported 5-year deal will keep Rice at Arsenal until 2031, into his early 30s. While the terms of the deal have yet to be signed, it is a huge statement from the club.

They are not only rewarding Rice for what he has done but also investing in what he can do.

With Arteta finding upcoming ways to utilise Rice’s qualities in midfield, Rice could still have some of his best years ahead of him.

Rafa Benitez has been talking about making a return to the Premier League.

The Spanish manager having previously been in charge at Liverpool, Chelsea, Newcastle United and Everton.

Rafa Benitez revealing that he has turned down a number of national team jobs in recent months, as well as clubs in both Mexico and Brazil.

The one-time Real Madrid boss telling The Athletic that now his priority is a Premier League job next.

Now 66, Rafa Benitez was sacked by Everton in 2022 and since then has only managed Celta Vigo and Panathinaikos.

The former Newcastle United manager lasting only nine months in Spain and eight months in Greece before getting the sack both times.

According to recent reports, rafa Benitez explaining to The Athletic: “For me, the priority is the Premier League. After you go Italy, Spain, Germany and France. In general, the Premier League has the most money and is able to buy the best players. You have some fantastic teams in Spain and Italy, but I like the atmosphere in the Premier League. I’m not just watching games; I’m analysing with a tactical vision, trying to learn something latest which I could implement. I don’t just want to be in a job; I want to be sure I can compete for something — whether that’s staying in the division, qualifying for Europe or winning something. I want to stay in Europe. Maybe I’ll have to go to China but that’s not the idea. There will come a point where if you cannot get what you want, you have to make a decision.”.

According to recent reports, rafa Benitez on how his future club would ideally look: “It has to be somewhere they respect your vision and experience…Are you creating something for the future? Is everyone on the same page? You need a clear vision and communication across the club, and time to improve a team. When you have had success in different countries, when you’ve had to handle difficult situations, when you know the mentality of players, you can manage in a different way and get the best out of them. Young people, especially, don’t attach too much value to experience, but after all these years, I’m a better coach than I’ve ever been.”.

During the interview, Rafa Benitez talked about his previous Premier League jobs and said about his time at Newcastle United under Mike Ashley: “We achieved something very difficult. We made a £30m profit (on player transfers) and won the Championship. Then we finished 10th and 13th in the Premier League without spending massive money. That was a great achievement.”.

There’s a massive catch however and West Ham will surely steer well clear after their experiences of blowing £27 million on a crocked Niclas Fullkrug who then spent a season and a half on the sick list.

Mateo Joseph – likely a long road ahead to regain match fitness.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that yesterday, it was confirmed that RedBird had rolled out the newly introduced holding firm to ‘consolidate RedBird’s Milan-based investments in sports, infrastructure, and entertainment’.
  • It has been revealed that brett Yormark has been appointed as the CEO of MSE after impressing as the Commissioner of the Significant 12 Conference (college sports), labelling it ‘an honour’ to get the position.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gerry Cardinale has commented on the launch of AC Milan’s upcoming holding tech giant, Milan Sports & Entertainment (MSE), stating that he will never sell the club.

Industry observers note that yesterday, it was confirmed that RedBird had rolled out the newly introduced holding firm to ‘consolidate RedBird’s Milan-based investments in sports, infrastructure, and entertainment’. From the new stadium to the NBA Europa project, there are substantial looks for the company.

It has been revealed that brett Yormark has been appointed as the CEO of MSE after impressing as the Commissioner of the Significant 12 Conference (college sports), labelling it ‘an honour’ to get the position. It doesn’t mean that we will see less of Cardinale though, quite the opposite.

Recent findings suggest that in an interview with Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Cardinale outlined exactly what he wants to achieve with MSE and explained why he will never sell the club. Silvio Berlusconi 2.0, as he calls it, with the goal of taking Milan back to the very top.

Cardinale, what benefits will AC Milan gain from the holding tech giant?

“The driving force behind deals like this is to provide AC Milan with the financial muscle needed to compete in the transfer market and secure the best players in the world.

“I will transform the club’s financial profile with the resources that will come from the stadium, the San Donato Arena, and the other activities we are working on with NBA Europe.

“I’m doing everything I can to ensure that, when we want a player, no one can tell me, ‘You can’t sign him because you can’t afford him.’ At the moment, only Premier League clubs are able to invest such sums and secure top players.

“If I want to bring AC Milan back to the top of European competition, not just in Italy, we need to figure out how to compete with the world’s top clubs.”.

This project confirms that your commitment to Milan is long-term….

Sources indicate that “Yes. I will never sell AC Milan. Never. And this is a project to get them back to winning ways. I’m not willing to tolerate it taking a long time to achieve this. I want to do it as soon as possible. We’ll see how rapidly….

Industry observers note that “My goal is to consistently win Scudetti and, of course, return to the Champions League. Milan Sports & Entertainment represents the foundation to make all this possible.”.

The connection with Milan deserves a separate mention: RedBird and the city are now even more connected….

In a recent development, “This is the legacy we will leave in Milan. The stadium, obviously, represents a huge legacy that will transform our financial profile, but then there’s also the San Donato development project and the rest.

“If we want AC Milan to become great again, we need to close the revenue gap with the Premier League clubs. When I bought the club four years ago, I used the expression ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ and no one understood what I meant. Now perhaps we are starting to see it.”.

Sources indicate that “Everyone thought I was making an arrogant, self-centred comparison between me and Berlusconi, but that wasn’t my point. What I was trying to explain was that, just as Berlusconi transformed AC Milan and Serie A, we want to be able, through our ownership, to lead the club into a latest era.

“We need to do it in the same way Berlusconi did, albeit in a modern way. I’m used to working a certain way because that’s how I do things, at the highest levels worldwide and in America.”.

Could your “recipe” also be valid for Serie A?

Sources indicate that “Of course, even for Serie A. In my opinion, it wouldn’t have been a good deal to sell 30% of the league’s international TV rights when JP Morgan made that offer. That’s not how Serie A can return to the top of Europe.

“It needs to be done through business planning and by creating every opportunity to generate new revenue. Like we will do with Milan Sports & Entertainment.

Sources indicate that “We will be the first to build a stadium since 2011, and that’s a huge achievement. I started working on it when I bought AC Milan, and finally… the right time has arrived.”.

Do you think others will follow you on this path?

Industry observers note that “No. Some may do it, others may not. We know what it takes to innovate and change. To avoid continuing to practice Einstein’s definition of insanity, according to which everyone wants a different outcome, but doesn’t want to do anything different to get it.”.

How long do you think it will take to complete the other projects that will be part of the new holding organization?

In a recent development, “I think the NBA is negotiating with the Euroleague, but one way or another, if they can’t reach an agreement, NBA Europe will still launch. Perhaps the first batch of new franchises for Europe will be unveiled at the end of the year or in early 2027.

“We will see when that happens… We own the land in San Donato, and if I’m granted the Milan franchise, I will be able to start construction fairly swiftly because we already have planning permission for a 20,000-seat arena.

“We will also continue to explore opportunities and hold discussions within the tennis world and to organise a tournament in Milan. Finally, we are already making progress in building and launching a hospitality and facility management tech giant.”.

Does your initiative include organising and managing hospitality services for other clubs’ stadiums as well, not just the new San Siro?

“Yes, the model is the manufacturer I created in 2009, called Legends Hospitality. I created it with the Latest York Yankees and the Dallas Cowboys. Now that company is worth several billion dollars.

“We not only sell premium seats, suites, merchandise, and hospitality, food, and beverage services for Yankee Stadium and Cowboys Stadium, but also for other clubs. I would like to adopt the same model here, probably in partnership with another club.”.

Not many football clubs in the world have established an organisation like the one you are leading….

Recent findings suggest that “Exactly. My ambition is to compete with the best clubs in the world. I want to do so thanks to my global vision of the world of sports and entertainment.

“There aren’t many multi-sports platforms in the world that also own some of their own facilities, and we want to add AC Milan to that list. To compete with them and then be better.”.

In a recent development, in an effort to generate new revenue, are you also considering a tour for AC Milan next summer? Will that still be Australia or the United States?

Recent findings suggest that “We have already discussed it with Amorim, and I will just tell you that if we play friendlies abroad, they will be in the United States next summer. If we do… We haven’t decided yet, and the decision will be up to Ruben.

Recent findings suggest that “It will depend on what’s best for the team: playing friendlies abroad must add value to the group, not bring in a couple of million for the club. Those extra two million will no longer be our goal, as they were under the previous management. That won’t happen again under this ownership.

Industry observers note that “Everything we organise in terms of friendlies will be carefully considered with our coach. Every move. And we won’t participate in tours organised by others. We put our players first. We want to help them prepare well to win. That’s our goal, and we aim to achieve it as soon as possible.”.

A dismayed mother and father spoke out after their 'elite' athlete twin sons were arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as they returned to their Alabama college.

Wallace State Community College soccer players Luis and Carlos Orta Santoro, 19, were taken into ICE custody after a traffic stop on November 4 while on their way to campus, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported.

The Venezuelan twins were returning from visiting their parents, Carlos Enrique Orta and Reyna Santoro de Orta, in Georgia when they were arrested by a Lincoln Police Department officer during a traffic stop in east-central Alabama.

The brothers graduated from Lawrenceville's Archer High School after a successful varsity soccer career that included a first ever region title for the school.

'This is the house of two elite soccer players,' Carlos Enrique Orta, their father, told the outlet.

Luis and Carlos are asylum seekers who applied for protections after legally entering the US on a tourist visa, like their parents.

That visa expired and the twins were granted US work permits and Georgia driver's licenses, according to the outlet.

A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, told the Daily Mail on Saturday that the brothers had legally entered the US with permission to stay on a temporary basis on June 21, 2022, but then 'illegally overstayed in defiance of our laws.'.

Twin brothers and soccer players Luis and Carlos Orta Santoro, both 19, were taken into ICE custody on November 5 after being arrested the previous day.

Luis and Carlos were region title-winning soccer players for Archer High School in Lawrenceville, Georgia.

The brothers were arrested as they returned from visiting their parents, Carlos Enrique Orta and Reyna Santoro de Orta (both left).

The DHS spokesperson told the Daily Mail: 'All their claims will be heard by an immigration judge, and they will receive due process. This administration will not ignore the rule of law.'.

'To be clear, pending applications do NOT confer legal status,' the statement continued.

Carlos was named the offensive player of the year and Luis the midfield player of the year by their high school this year.

They had received soccer scholarships to attend Wallace State, which they began doing this fall, but now face deportation to Venezuela.

'It's been hell,' Santoro de Orta, their mother, told the outlet.

She added that she supported ICE 'taking away the criminals' but stated her children did not fit that description.

A final decision on the brothers' asylum case is still pending as they remain in custody.

The concerned mother claimed police said the twins' car had failed to come to a complete stop at a stop sign.

The brothers were arrested by a Lincoln Police Department officer as they were returning to Wallace State Community College, where they have soccer scholarships.

The family applied for asylum protections after legally entering the country on a tourist visa. The DHS said the brothers 'illegally overstayed in defiance of our laws'.

The Lincoln Police Department signed a partnership agreement with ICE in July.

ICE mentioned the program allows trained local officers to exercise limited immigration authority during routine police work under federal supervision, according to the Cullman Tribune.

Luis and Carlos were booked into the Talladega County Jail on November 4 and transferred to ICE custody the following day.

Their father, Orta, described how the family was grappling with guilt as they shared what happened to their children.

Sources indicate that 'If anyone is at fault, it's me. It's us,' Orta told the outlet. 'Because I insist and I will continue to insist that Carlos and Luis came here because of a decision we made.'.

He added: 'Carlos and Luis stayed here because of a decision from mom and dad. Carlos and Luis are here because of us.'.

The brothers have been taken to the the Pine Prairie ICE Processing Center in southern Louisiana.

A friend of the twins, Nicolas Azcarate Florez, noted he had spoken to them multiple times since they were taken into custody.

'They've been saying that they've been moved five times, so it has been difficult for them,' Azcarate Florez told the outlet.

Azcarate Florez stated the brothers were 'players that you could just give the ball to, and you would know that they would do something good with it.'.

'If we needed them, we would know that they would be there to help us out of a sticky situation,' he added.

The brothers were taken into custody on the same week that the Republican Party faced a historic blue wave in the midterm elections that was seen as a rebuke of the GOP's immigration policy.

One of President Donald Trump's first moves afterwards was to name Stephen Miller as the newly introduced White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles.

Miller, one of Trump's most loyal and longest-serving advisers going back to his first administration, is known for his hardline views on immigration.

Critics have cited Miller as the architect of some of Trump's most divisive policies, including separating migrant families during deportations in the President's first term.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Viktor Gyökeres is reminding Arsenal of his prolific goal scoring capabilities.

The striker found the back of the net twice in Sweden’s 3-2 Nations League win against Bosnia and Herzegovina on November 14, both times from the spot to take his total to four in the Nations League this season.

The win also means they have booked their place in League A with one match left to play in the group, and Gyökeres has certainly played his part in this excellent run.

Recent findings suggest that however, the performance will raise questions about his future at the club. The idea that he may be leaving in January is a possibility that needs to be looked at.

There is a stark difference between his international and club form.

Gyökeres has only played 181 minutes in seven Premier League games this season, starting just once as Kai Havertz has usually been preferred in central areas.

Recent findings suggest that however, he has had more opportunities to play in European competition. Gyökeres has started three of Arsenal’s four matches in the Champions League, scoring one goal and providing two assists.

Gyökeres is not totally out of Arteta’s aims, but he will not play much domestically.

He has been in fine form internationally recently. Sweden are building their attack around his movement and penalty area presence, meaning he will have chances to regularly perform.

Recent findings suggest that however, just because he is doing well internationally does not mean he will start regularly for the club. Arteta has other attacking options and tactics to consider.

There have been suggestions surrounding Gyökeres’ future, with reports that Arsenal may look to add more attacking flair to their squad.

AC Milan and Juventus have also been linked, but there is no agreement or suggestion that either club is looking to make a January move for the forward.

Gyökeres has opened up about the speculation.

According to recent reports, in an interview with Swedish media outlet Fotbollskanalen during the international break, he stated that he would like to stay at the club. The player also denied any concerns with his relationship with Arteta, stating that they have good communication.

Industry observers note that however, the player may not stay forever, as he has not played much in the Premier League so far. If this continues, and Arsenal sign another forward, it could cause an issue.

For now, though, there is little evidence that Gyökeres is trying to leave the club.

It has been revealed that he’ll be looking to get regular game time at 28 after finding his scoring touch with Sweden. Arsenal will also need to work out how to use him best as a goalscoring striker.

But for now the January speculation seems a little early. He has stated he wants to stay at Arsenal, and the next few weeks may prove to be more notable.

#14636. Why Newcastle United the football club is an entity which I find increasingly loathsome

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1857 w)

Why Newcastle United the football club is an entity which I find increasingly loathsome

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1857 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over nearly forty years of supporting Newcastle United, there are few things more certain than the knowledge that this club will let me down time and again.
  • In a recent development, in terms of what happens on the field, that is part and parcel of being a football supporter.
  • To that end, on the law of averages we are very fortunate to support a club that has spent its entire existence in the top two tiers of English football, most of my lifetime in the top division and even won a trophy a couple of years back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over nearly forty years of supporting Newcastle United, there are few things more certain than the knowledge that this club will let me down time and again.

In a recent development, in terms of what happens on the field, that is part and parcel of being a football supporter. After all, there are 92 league clubs and it stands to reason that the vast majority of those teams will only watch on, frustrated, while a small minority achieve success.

To that end, on the law of averages we are very fortunate to support a club that has spent its entire existence in the top two tiers of English football, most of my lifetime in the top division and even won a trophy a couple of years back.

So in that context, you can be pragmatic about the failures, enjoy the successes when they come and proudly tell the players in black and white that “we’ll support you ever more”.

In a recent development, yet it is the club’s activity off the field that really gets my goat. I hate to say it, but while the club has stabilised since the takeover, improved as a commercial entity and enjoyed a bit of silverware for the first time in forever, it has also lost its soul.

“Our fans are the beating heart of Newcastle United,” declared CEO David Hopkinson as he declared the latest season ticket price hike earlier this year.

In 2025, he told the Newcastle United Supporters Trust: “Supporters are at the heart of everything we do.” Meanwhile, chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan claimed our support “will never be taken for granted” in an open letter to fans back in 2022.

None of this is true though, is it?

We are absolutely taken for granted. And if we are at the heart of what the club does, it is in the most transactional sense possible – as paying lemmings who are a guaranteed source of income.

Take my experience of trying to get tickets for my sons for the Sunderland game as a prime example.

To be clear, I fully understand that match tickets are at a premium and for this game more than any other, demand would have been huge.

Imagine my surprise, then, when my two sons were seemingly successful in the ballot.

Given the club claim it is a strike rate of one in seven yet this was my eldest son’s first successful ballot in 22 attempts and my youngest son’s first in 15, this was a particularly welcome stroke of luck.

Worse still, because we tried to have him accompany my elder son in the family area, neither were allowed to utilise their ballot success, as my eldest was automatically disqualified when he no longer had a youth to accompany him.

Now I totally understand why these rules exist. Our situation was an unfortunate quirk of when my youngest son’s birthday fell and was an error made in good faith, but it would be very easy for people to exploit this and fill the family section with adults if the club were not vigilant. I get that and I respect that.

That is why I accept when I phoned the Box Office to try to resolve this unforeseen anomaly they were unable to provide us with tickets in that area.

What was less easy to accept was the absolute wall of intransigence and unhelpfulness I was faced with.

Industry observers note that could we get tickets in a different area? “No, you’ve won the ballot in that area so that’s it”.

Why does the website block us from buying the tickets now but did not block us from entering a ballot that it turns out we could never win? “It is your responsibility to enter the ballot in the right area.”.

Industry observers note that can we not just have two tickets elsewhere given that the allocation that goes on general sale will be unchanged – we will not be using the two we have won so it will be the same net figure? “No, the policy does not allow that. It would not be fair on other supporters.”.

The ballot system is inherently unfair as our strike rate highlights – we have had a rare success and now we cannot use it because the system allowed us to enter a ballot we could not win. Is that fair? “I’m not prepared to depart from the policy.”.

As anyone who has encountered our Supporter Services will know, escalating the matter to them was about as effective as the experiment of playing Nick Woltemade as a number 8.

Some will say I should not base my view of the club on interactions with a handful of lower paid staff working in the Box Office and Supporter Services. I disagree.

According to recent reports, senior leaders in any organisation set the culture. If David Hopkinson truly believed supporters are the “beating heart” of Newcastle United, he and his executive team would have led the behaviours that set the tone for everyone else.

Interactions with the frontline staff are the very best test for what an organisation really values, and I can tell you now that Newcastle United does not value its supporters beyond the transactional purpose they serve.

Industry observers note that allow me to give another example. Last season, my sister won two tickets in the ballot to take her son to see Newcastle play Bournemouth.

Industry observers note that now my sister is a proper fan. Growing up in Hexham, she spent most of her teen years trying to hang around Causey Hill in Hexham long enough to wave at the passing cars of Mick Quinn, Ray Ranson, Kevin Brock and Mark McGhee, who lived at the top of the road. She even became Roy Aitken’s family babysitter!

She started going to games during the desperate 1988-89 season which ended in relegation and has been a regular at home and away games ever since.

Now living in the south east, getting to home games is an effort and the Bournemouth game last season proved to be a particular trial.

Train delay after train delay resulted in that trip becoming akin to the Griswalds’ trip to Wally World in National Lampoon’s Vacation: rather than it being a day out, it became a mission.

After the first delay they knew it would be tight for kick-off, by the second they knew they would miss some of the first half, by the next they were hoping to get in for the second half, and by the time they eventually arrived it was a case of: “We’ve come this far, we might as well watch the last 10 minutes!”.

Recent findings suggest that off they bombed sprinting up Pink Lane to get to the ground, only to arrive in around the 80th minute and be turned away by the stewards. They presented their tickets, they told them what they had been through, but it was all to no avail. Supporter Services on the day were actually very supportive; those based at the ground stated the stewards had made the wrong call and if they called up on Monday they would “see what they could do.”.

It turned out, what they could do was never tested: what they would do was absolutely nothing. Supporter Services denied any knowledge of the response they had been given on the Saturday, and virtually accused my sister of making the whole thing up.

“Supporters are at the heart of everything we do”, are they Mr Hopkinson? Well that is not the experience most of us face when interacting with the people you field to manage those relationships.

No, this is a club which has lost its heart.

Sources indicate that you need look no further than the utterly dreadful rendition of Blaydon Races which they have forced us to endure on matchdays to understand quite how much the decision-makers at Newcastle United do not understand what our club is. What used to set us apart in home games was the intensity and atmosphere that the crowd brought. Messrs Keegan, Robson and Howe all understood that.

When I was at the depressing Everton game recently, I could not help but think immediately before kick-off ahead of both the first and second halves how the people who make those decisions are strangling the life out of what we are.

If ever there was a way to sap the atmosphere out of the crowd when you need them most it would be by drowning them out with a funeral-march rendition of the Geordie anthem being played at full blast through the stadium speakers. It even killed the Strawberry Corner.

You look at other things – like that dreadful variation on our club badge – and wonder what on earth motivates these people to make the decisions that they do.

I mean, seriously, was it worth the upset and cost of changing a crest we have known and loved for decades just to introduce that abomination?

According to recent reports, I will always love Newcastle United, because it is part of me. That is why, despite Yasir Al-Rummayan’s protestations to the contrary, it is so easy for the powers that be to take us for granted, which they do unreservedly and indiscriminately. We are hooked in by the nostalgia, the memories, the stories, the glorious moments.

Maybe we are motivated by that truly united feeling of togetherness when you are packed into the concourse at any away ground, chanting for 20 minutes non-stop just for each other and the looks on the faces of the bemused home stewards because there’s not a player or opposition supporter in sight.

Perhaps we are driven by the hope, or the sheer unbridled joy of that last-minute winner or a hard-fought victory against one of the league’s elite.

Or for some of us it is just a way of life. Something we did with our mum or dad and now we do with our children, and one day when they are mums and dads they will do with their children too.

In more crass terms, a cynic might say we are victims of Stockholm Syndrome: a condition in which people develop an emotional attachment, affection or loyalty to their captor or abuser.

Sources indicate that however much we love Newcastle United, we should never be allow ourselves to forget that it is a love which is utterly unrequited. We are commodities to buy tickets, buy shirts and create an image of fervour that can be sold as a commercial package to the highest bidder.

Sources indicate that the members’ general sale tickets for Sunderland sold out within minutes. Yet there is still plenty of room if you are prepared to pay £800 for your ticket, along with  bit of food and the brief musings of one of Keegan’s Entertainers pre and post-match.

While Newcastle United the football team remains something I seem bound to unconditionally love despite all my senses telling me I should not, Newcastle United the football club is an entity which I find increasingly loathsome.
