📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

Sources indicate that ONE-TOUCH BRILLIANCE! ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No. 125, goal No. 90 for the skipper 👏 https://t.co/otMcxlXyps.

Following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

Hall ➡️ Kane! The Newcastle fullback swings in the corner and it's the England captain who rises highest to head home 💥 https://t.co/5EhAcNZUqm.

Afterwards at a Wembley press conference to mark the occasion, he invoked the cricket analogy himself on the question of scoring 100 England goals. “Being in the 90s, I try not to think about it too much, and it’s like I guess being a cricketer in the 90s. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

At the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he stated. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”.

One expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

“Availability,” he said, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

No team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. Tuchel’s name was sung at Wembley and even if the World Cup semi-final collapse in Atlanta in July has not been entirely forgotten, the roughest edges have been taken off somewhat. Another great performance from Jude Bellingham and also from Morgan Rogers, in place of Bukayo Saka. Another dominant Elliot Anderson performance in midfield. They left Wembley to applause and a sense of optimism renewed.

England kept the ball with such authority, and none more so than Bellingham. Trent Alexander-Arnold came back at right-back. Myles Lewis-Skelly returned for another bite at a Wembley midfield job. As in Prague last week, there was a self-inflicted Czech calamity in the first half. The captain Vladimir Coufal appeared to lose his cool at the threat of the England attack all over the Czechs’ half. No other reason for this Premier League experienced full-back to fling himself at Kane’s cross and drill the ball past Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek on 27 minutes.

It has been revealed that england lead! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿⚽️ A great ball from Kane and a great finish from Coufal - unfortunately for the defender, it's in the wrong net...🫣 https://t.co/h54xQnunZM.

It has been revealed that the second goal, on 40 minutes, was one for the ages. Anderson’s ball out to the right was met first time by Rogers for the cross and Kane ran into the space, as he has done so many times, to deliver a finish struck with customary assuredness. Bellingham almost flicked in Rogers’s cross on 56 minutes and from the corner that came after, Kane nodded in a header at the back post from Lewis Hall’s cross. All remarked, the defending was woeful but there was nothing wrong with the finish.

Thomas Tuchel believes England have taken a step forward from their World Cup heartbreak over this international break and said he was “honoured” to hear fans sing his name.

England finished their four Nations League games with a 3-0 win over Czech Republic, in which Harry Kane scored twice on his record-equalling 125th appearance.

It meant that Tuchel’s team have won three and lost one, against Spain, of their four games since the World Cup, after which the England head coach was heavily criticised for the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Tuchel seems to have won the forgiveness of some England supporters, who sang his name at the start and the end of Tuesday’s game.

Sources indicate that “It means a lot,” Tuchel said. “It’s amazing to have a song. It’s the biggest honour. And I’m very happy and very honoured. They can be sure that I will give my absolute best to make our team win and play well.”.

Asked if he sensed a change in mood around his England team since the fall-out from the World Cup, Tuchel noted: “I do and I think it’s necessary to move on. I think I can only repeat that we didn’t go out in the group stage. Sometimes it feels like that and we didn’t. As I said, our aim was always to progress, move forward and improve.”.

Tuchel snapped back at a reporter who questioned why he felt it necessary to repeat that England had not gone out in the group stage of the World Cup, claiming the criticism had felt a “little bit” too harsh.

Industry observers note that but on whether England have shown they are a step ahead of where the team were at the World Cup during this international camp, Tuchel was far more positive and replied: “Of course and that’s what we have to do. That is our goal to constantly improve and develop.

“We had these experiences together and we had a massive tournament together, and it was very positive. It’s necessary to move forward and improve, especially in sports. This is what we’re trying to do.

Recent findings suggest that “We adjusted some details in our structure and we didn’t compromise on the effort and the intensity, and on the togetherness of the team. The players who were with us in the World Cup took care of these standards and of the culture within the team, off the pitch and on the pitch, and I think that’s what you could see.”.

Recent findings suggest that we played a very good match, very fluid and to put it into context it was the fourth match in 11 or 12 days. We dominated the whole match, had some good opportunities, scored some beautiful goals. Subs were strong. Very good performance again.

[Leading the way, Mr Kane] Of course. That’s what he does. I don’t take it for granted. It’s just exceptional, every single match. It’s just difficult to find latest words to express it.

Training, attitude, cohesion, belief, of course [is why they’re stronger than ever].

Recent findings suggest that [Has the World Cup made England stronger?]  Of course, we got the first medal in 60 years. We didn’t go out in the group stage. We grew stronger.

In a recent development, I was happy that everyone who was in the camp was contributing. Everyone was on the pitch. Good evening and welcome to live coverage of England vs Czech Republic from Wembley in the fourth and mercifully final round of fixtures in this sprawling Nations League international break. Tonight Harry Kane will win his 125th cap and equal Peter Shilton for England appearances.

In a recent development, shilton’s took him 20 years as Gordon Banks was simply too good in the couple of years following his debut and then a couple of managers, Don Revie and Ron Greenwood, preferred Ray Clemence until the latter finally plumped for Shilton as No 1 in 1979. Kane’s, by contrast, have taken him 11. In that time he has been rested for a handful of friendlies but has not been unused in a competitive match when fit since Gareth Southgate left him out of the 5-0 victory over Sam Marino in 2021’s World Cup qualifier when Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored two and Ollie Watkins one goal on his debut.

They went on to marmalise Croatia 7-0 in their next game in front of a crowd that sounded like a cross between the choirs on Another Brick in the Wall, Part 2 and There’s No One Quite Like Grandma.

In the past England have had problems backing up their best performances – the 4-1 evisceration of the Dutch at Euro 96 was followed by the cagey display in the quarter-final against Spain before prevailing on penalties, the 5-1 victory in Munich in 2001 led to a drab 2-0 win against Albania at St James’ Park the following Tuesday, in 2016 they went to Berlin and beat world champions Germany but were thumped by Netherlands, who had not even qualified for Euro 2016, a couple of days later. Even their thrilling, second-half showing against Croatia in their World Cup opener in June preceded the dreary 0-0 draw with Ghana.

Given the attacking fluency in Rijeka, Thomas Tuchel must be tempted not to to ring the changes and replace seven or eight players. He will have to find replacements for the injured Alex Scott and Ezri Konsa, however, and Calvert Lewin, who has had seven minutes of action, Rio Ngumoha 19, Morgan Gibbs-White 27 and Jarrad Branthwaite one, may feel they deserve a fairer opportunity to show what they can do in a match.

Sources indicate that china’s one-child policy is probably the best-known population-control programme in history, yet in its first decade it barely changed the country’s fertility rate. Writing in Nature, Meng et al.1 show that the biggest drop in fertility after the policy’s introduction was driven by a change in how officials were incentivized to enforce it. This change accounts for about half of the fall in the country’s fertility rate during the 1990s.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jamie Carragher has urged Liverpool to be active in the January transfer window if ‘a certain type’ of player becomes attainable.

The Reds have made some major mid-season signings in the past, with Virgil van Dijk, Daniel Sturridge, Luis Suarez, Philippe Coutinho and Luis Diaz all joining in the winter months, but they haven’t entered the January market for an immediate latest addition since landing Cody Gakpo nearly four years ago.

The window will open in just over six weeks’ time, so speculation over prospective new arrivals will no doubt intensify in the lead-up to New Year’s, and Carragher feels that his former club must be proactive if they spot the right market opportunity.

Speaking on The Overlap Fan Debate, the ex-Liverpool defender mentioned: “For me, this season for [Andoni] Iraola is about making sure we’re in a position for next season to really challenge for the title, so I think every transfer window is rightly notable.

“The areas on the pitch for Liverpool that still stand out for me – and we’ve got Hugo Ekitike to come back as well, so that’ll fix the back-up for Alexander Isak, or maybe play alongside Isak – is the full-back area.

According to recent reports, “If there’s a left-back, they’ve got to go and do it in January. Or a midfield player, a certain type of midfield player. It’s not about what we did with [Jurgen] Klopp, where we’d wait for the summer, because this feels like it’s the here and now.”.

One thing the Reds have proven quite adept at in previous Januarys is making a late surge to snare a mid-season signing, like they did when stealing in for Diaz in 2022 and Gakpo the following winter.

It’s notable that the Dutchman was signed when Julian Ward was Liverpool’s sporting director, and he’s now back in that job title for a second spell, having shown in the past that he’s prepared to pounce for the right opportunity.

Recent findings suggest that carragher’s reservations about the full-back berths are understandable. Both Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley on the right have been hampered by injury concerns, while Kostas Tsimikas hasn’t been able to provide stern competition for Milos Kerkez on the other flank.

LFC won’t enter the January market for the sake of it and won’t be swayed by external opinion, no matter how voluble it might be, but that isn’t to say that they definitely won’t bring in a latest signing or two during the winter window.

Liverpool’s transfer strategy could also be swayed by what happens over the coming weeks, and whether they go into the Fresh Year with Andoni Iraola worryingly light in some positions.

Carragher is spot-on about one thing – if there’s a smart deal to be done in January, then Ward must swoop in straight away rather than biding his time for next summer.

  • The following season, it was as if things had changed completely, as the centre-back started performing really well and was rewarded with a lot of playing time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mario Gila has explained how he managed to get through a difficult time at the start of his Italy adventure, eventually performing at such a high level that AC Milan decided to sign him.

In a recent development, gila left Real Madrid and Spain in the summer of 2022, when he was just 21 years old, as Lazio secured his services. In his first season, however, he only got 765 minutes on the pitch and didn’t play a single game in the second half of the campaign.

The following season, it was as if things had changed completely, as the centre-back started performing really well and was rewarded with a lot of playing time. The growth only continued from there, resulting in Milan paying good money for him in the summer.

Industry observers note that in his long interview with AC Milan for the interview series The Chamber, Gila discussed his initial struggles in Italy, hitting ‘rock bottom’ in his first season with Lazio. A psychologist and a changed mindset helped him get through it all.

In a recent development, when you make a mistake, are you very demanding and hard on yourself? I mean, how do you treat yourself when something doesn’t go the way you wanted?

Recent findings suggest that “In the past, for example… I’ve changed a great deal. I went through a really difficult time early in my career here in Italy and hit rock bottom, but with outside help, psychological support, I got through it.

It has been revealed that “That’s why I keep saying ‘before’. Back then, I was very hard on myself. I didn’t allow myself to fail. If I did, I was extremely negative towards myself, I couldn’t accept that I might fail or make mistakes.

“Now I handle it much better. Now I feel that making mistakes is part of the job, it’s something that helps you improve, something that helps you grow. So I deal with it much more calmly, I process it much better internally.

“I think you still need to hold yourself to high standards and you also need to know how to find a solution to that mistake, whether in your career or in your personal life, but with much more calm and more kindness towards myself.”.

It has been revealed that regarding that difficult period you went through, which helped you grow and taught you so many things, you mentioned therapy. Could you tell me, not so much what happened, but what your experience with therapy was like? I mean, what did it give you at first?

“I sought help from a psychologist because I was going through a very difficult time and couldn’t find a way to move forward. We’re expected to deal with situations… that I find mentally overwhelming, at just 21 years old, when you have no professional experience, because in the end, everything comes at you so fast.

According to recent reports, “So I went to a psychologist, and completely changed my perspective. I mean, I started seeing everything negative that happened to me as a step forward, thinking: this is something that will help you improve, something you needed to go through.

Sources indicate that “Everything changed when I changed my perspective. I used to be very hard on myself, very hard, I demanded so much of myself. Now I’m someone who feels much more at ease.

“We can all fail, make mistakes, go through difficult situations, So the way I treat myself, the way I respond to myself, the way I talk to myself, I think it plays a crucial role in maintaining a consistently positive mindset.”.

  • The Scorpions suffered their first defeat of the campaign in Thursday's meeting in Bouake, going down 2-1 to the Elephants, and now face another stern test against the three-time African champions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 15 Nov 2026 15:11.

Gambia will be looking to keep their hopes of qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations alive when they welcome Group C leaders Ivory Coast to the Independence Stadium in Bakau for the second leg of their double-header on Tuesday, five days after losing the opening encounter.

The Scorpions suffered their first defeat of the campaign in Thursday's meeting in Bouake, going down 2-1 to the Elephants, and now face another stern test against the three-time African champions.

Ivory Coast have made an impressive start to their qualifying campaign, winning all three matches to collect nine points and move three clear of second-placed Gambia.

Herve Renard's side opened their campaign with a 2-0 victory over Ghana before recording another 2-0 success against Somalia, and a fast start in Bouake on Thursday allowed them to maintain their perfect record.

The Elephants moved two goals ahead inside the opening 24 minutes through Malick Yalcouye's opener and Elye Wahi's strike before Musa Barrow reduced the deficit with a long-range effort in the 38th minute.

Renard has now guided his side to three wins from four outings since returning to the Ivory Coast dugout for a second spell in August following the Elephants' round-of-32 exit at the World Cup, with their only setback during that period a 1-0 friendly defeat to Cameroon in October.

One win away from securing qualification for the continental finals, the Frenchman, who led the Ivorians to AFCON glory in 2015, will be eager to complete the job on Tuesday and guide his team to a 27th appearance at the tournament.

Gambia, meanwhile, are bidding to reach the AFCON finals for only the third time, having previously featured in the 2021 and 2023 editions, and they did make an encouraging start to their qualifying campaign.

Having collected six points from their opening three matches, the Scorpions, who right now sit second in the group, beat Somalia in round one before recovering from two goals down to defeat Ghana 4-2, leaving Thursday's setback in Bouake as their only blemish so far.

Johnny McKinstry's team have been prolific in the final third, scoring seven times across their three qualifying matches, more than any other side in Group C, although their defensive record has been less convincing, with five goals conceded.

Indeed, the Scorpions have failed to keep a clean sheet in each of their last six outings across all competitions, shipping two or more goals in five of those games and conceding 13 in total, a record that offers little encouragement against visitors who have scored twice in every qualifying fixture.

With another defeat potentially putting their chances at risk, particularly as third-placed Ghana, who trail by three points, face bottom side Somalia, the hosts will hope to draw confidence from losing just once in their last six home matches (W2, D3).

However, the Scorpions must also contend with a poor head-to-head record, having lost each of their previous five meetings with Ivory Coast, with Thursday's defeat yielding their only goal during that run.

Ivory Coast Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Ivory Coast form (all competitions):.

Gambia will again be without Alieu Fadera and Adama Sidibeh, while Jesper Ceesay and Suleiman Camara were also unavailable for the double-header after reportedly withdrawing from the squad through injury.

Barrow and Yankuba Minteh have returned after missing September's qualifiers through injury, with the former finding the net in Bouake and the latter featuring after the interval.

Twenty-one-year-old forward Alasana Yirajang remains under disciplinary sanction from the country's FA, having missed the first leg and set to serve a further two-match ban.

Ivory Coast remain without Odilon Kossounou, Guela Doue and Ghislain Konan, who have been unavailable through injury, while Ange-Yoan Bonny withdrew from the squad before the opening encounter.

Emmanuel Agbadou was also carrying a knee problem ahead of Thursday's fixture, although Oumar Solet has since received FIFA approval to represent the Elephants and is eligible for the return meeting.

Wahi is expected to lead the line again after scoring his first international goal, although it remains to be seen whether Renard will rotate his attacking options after Real Madrid's Yan Diomande and Nicolas Pepe provided support from the flanks.

Manchester United winger Amad Diallo featured in a three-man midfield alongside Nottingham Forest's Ibrahim Sangare and Brighton & Hove Albion's Malick Junior Yalcouye, although captain Franck Kessie could earn a starting berth after coming on as a substitute last time out.

Gambia possible starting lineup:.

Gaye; Saine, Ceesay, O Colley, Y Bojang, Toureay; E Colley, Bajo, Adams, Barrow; Badamosi.

Ivory Coast possible starting lineup:.

Fofana; Zogbe, O Diomande, Ndicka, Kamara; Kessie, Sangare, Yalcouye; Diallo, Wahi, Y Diomande.

The Gambia should benefit from playing in front of their own supporters and possess enough attacking threat to trouble the visitors, but Ivory Coast's stronger qualifying record and greater squad depth could prove decisive, making an away victory the more likely outcome.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 15 Nov 2026 15:54, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 11:37.

In a battle for automatic promotion, Hungary's clash with visitors Northern Ireland at Puskas Arena on Tuesday will decide which team secures first place in their Nations League B group.

Both are certain of a top two finish heading into the final matchday, with second-placed Hungary on 10 points and first-placed Northern Ireland on 11, but only top spot guarantees promotion into League A.

Hungary managed to defeat Georgia 2-0 on Saturday, though they needed an own goal from Lasha Dvali to open the scoring in the 73rd minute.

That was the country's third consecutive triumph in the Nations League, with the hosts keeping two clean sheets while scoring five goals in that stretch.

Manager Marco Rossi will know that his side have secured a promotion playoff spot, but that would require them to navigate a two-legged tie against one of the two lowest-ranked third-placed teams or one of the two highest-ranked fourth-placed teams from League A.

Magyars have only lost one of their last nine games in all competitions, winning on six occasions, though they were held to a goalless stalemate by Northern Ireland on September 29.

Hungary's record at home has also been strong, with the country having emerged as victors in four of their six most recent contests when designated as hosts.

Northern Ireland beat Ukraine 1-0 on Saturday thanks to a long-range strike from wing-back Terry Devlin, and that has put them on the verge of Nations League A for the first time.

A draw would make certain of their progression into the top division, and the visitors will be confident considering the only loss they have suffered in their past eight matches was against France in June (W4, D3, L1).

Green and White Army only managed to score more than one goal in one of those eight fixtures, netting exactly one goal five times.

Head coach Michael O'Neill will be pleased that his country have only been beaten in one of their last four meetings with Hungary, winning once, but their hosts have beaten them in five of their eight encounters.

Northern Ireland have won both of their away clashes in their Nations League group, but they were defeated in six of their prior eight contests on the road.

Hungary form (all competitions):.

Northern Ireland Nations League form:.

Northern Ireland form (all competitions):.

Hungary captain Dominik Szoboszlai revealed that he almost picked up an injury in the buildup to their clash with Georgia, though he insisted that he was willing to battle through in order to make it into the XI on Tuesday.

The midfielder could be used in an advanced role ahead of Rajmund Toth and Andras Schafer, especially as Milan Vitalis is suspended.

Centre-back Attila Szalai may have to be thrown into the backline due to Willi Orban's suspension, while Barnabas Varga will hope to score a 17th international goal.

Northern Ireland forward Jamie Donley led the line against Ukraine, but after picking up a yellow card, he will miss Tuesday's clash.

Perhaps Josh Magennis will be trusted to start as a striker, stationed between wide forwards Ethan Galbraith and Isaac Price, while Shea Charles will marshal midfield.

Hungary possible starting lineup:.

B Toth; Osvath, Szalai, Csinger, Kerkez; R Toth, Schafer; Sallai, Szoboszlai, Nagy; Varga.

Northern Ireland possible starting lineup:.

P Charles; Atcheson, McConville, Brown; Devlin, Hume, S Charles, Devenny; Galbraith, Magennis, Price.

Northern Ireland have been difficult to beat for some time, and Hungary already failed to get the better of them in the group stage.

Though the visitors may not have enough in attack to win, they should have enough to take a point, especially as the hosts are missing key starters.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 15 Nov 2026 16:06.
  • Togo will be looking to revive their hopes of reaching the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations when they welcome Algeria to the Stade de Kegue in Lome for the second meeting between the sides in the space of three days on Tuesday.
  • The Sparrowhawks suffered a narrow 1-0 defeat in Saturday's encounter in Tizi Ouzou, a result that leaves them third in Group I, one point behind second-placed Zambia and four adrift of section leaders Algeria.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 15 Nov 2026 16:06.

Togo will be looking to revive their hopes of reaching the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations when they welcome Algeria to the Stade de Kegue in Lome for the second meeting between the sides in the space of three days on Tuesday.

The Sparrowhawks suffered a narrow 1-0 defeat in Saturday's encounter in Tizi Ouzou, a result that leaves them third in Group I, one point behind second-placed Zambia and four adrift of section leaders Algeria.

Algeria head into the return fixture in a strong position after collecting seven points from their opening three Group I matches (W2, D1) under upcoming coach Ibrahim Hamdani, who replaced Vladimir Petkovic following his departure in August.

The Desert Foxes began their qualifying campaign with a 3-1 victory over Zambia before recovering from two goals down to draw 2-2 with Burundi, and they maintained their unbeaten record by edging Togo in their most recent outing.

Hemdani's side had to work hard for Saturday's victory, with Ramy Bensebaini heading home from an Anis Hadj Moussa cross in the 76th minute after the hosts had struggled to turn their early pressure into goals.

The result extended Algeria's unbeaten run under Hemdani to four matches since their World Cup round-of-32 exit, having also recorded a friendly victory over Niger in October.

A win on Tuesday would secure the Desert Foxes a place at their 22nd AFCON finals with two games to spare, although they have managed just one victory in their last four matches outside Algeria (D1, L2).

Togo, meanwhile, are aiming to reach the AFCON finals for the first time since 2017, having made a winning start to their qualifying campaign against Burundi before suffering back-to-back defeats without scoring.

Patrice Neveu's team were beaten 2-0 by Zambia in the second round of qualifiers, while their latest loss in Algeria means they have now lost consecutive matches for the first time since falling to Senegal and Mauritania in March and September 2025, respectively.

Saturday's result also extended Togo's poor record in this fixture, having lost seven of their last eight meetings with Algeria across all competitions, including a 1-0 defeat in their most recent home encounter during the 2025 AFCON qualifiers.

However, victories in four of their last seven competitive matches on home soil (D2, L1) offer some encouragement, particularly as a win on Tuesday could lift them into second place if Zambia drop points against Burundi.

Togo  Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Algeria  Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Algeria form (all competitions):.

Algeria have several absentees to contend with, with Jaouen Hadjam, Amine Chiakha, Rafik Belghali, Hicham Boudaoui and Bachir Belloumi all ruled out through injury.

Goalkeeper Abdelatif Ramdane also left the camp following the death of his father, with Fahem Benaissa-Yahia, Rayane Yesli, Adem Zorgane and Saadi Radouani called up as replacements.

Bensebaini has now scored the decisive goal in each of Algeria's last two meetings with Togo, and the left-back will be keen to make another contribution in the attacking third.

Togo will again be without Sharani Zuberu, Mansour Ouro-Tagba and Steven Nador, who withdrew from the squad before the first meeting, with Gustave Akueson and Yaw Annor called up as replacements.

Lilian Brassier made his international debut in Saturday's defeat and could retain his place in defence after putting in a solid display.

Barcola; Nadjombe, Drakpe, Boateng, Brassier, Koudossou; Ouro, Djene, Denkey, Karim; Laba.

Algeria possible starting lineup:.

Mastil; Azzi, Abada, Touba, Bensebaini; H Moussa, Bentaleb, Maza, Chaibi; Gouiri, Amoura.

Togo indicated in the first meeting that they can trouble Algeria, but their lack of goals remains a major concern, particularly against opponents who have continued to find ways to collect results despite several absentees.

The hosts should make this a competitive encounter in front of their supporters, but Algeria's recent dominance in this fixture could help them secure another victory.

#14528. Malawi vs Egypt - prediction, team news, lineups

Malawi vs Egypt - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (730 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Adepoju Marvellous | 15 Nov 2026 16:22, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 16:33.
  • Group B leaders Egypt travel to Bingu National Stadium on Tuesday to face Malawi in round four of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.
  • The record winners will secure their place at next year’s showpiece with a victory, while Malawi must avoid defeat to keep their slim qualification hopes alive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 15 Nov 2026 16:22, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 16:33.

Group B leaders Egypt travel to Bingu National Stadium on Tuesday to face Malawi in round four of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

The record winners will secure their place at next year’s showpiece with a victory, while Malawi must avoid defeat to keep their slim qualification hopes alive.

Egypt’s Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign began with a disappointing goalless draw against Angola - a result that saw the seven-time champions fail to secure maximum points in their opening qualifier for the first time since 2019.

A 5-0 win over Malawi in the following match put the Pharaohs back on track, but it proved to be Hossam Hassan’s last competitive game in charge before he was dismissed amid controversy surrounding his relationship with his ex-wife.

New coach Ali Maher enjoyed a dream start, overseeing a 5-0 victory over Malawi at Cairo International Stadium on Friday to put Egypt on the verge of a sixth straight AFCON appearance, having inexplicably missed three consecutive editions between 2012 and 2015.

Egypt are yet to concede a goal in qualifying and have scored a tournament-high 10 goals, with that solidity on both ends of the pitch boding well for a side aiming to end a 17-year wait for continental glory since winning three consecutive titles.

Last Friday’s win in Cairo marked Egypt’s fifth consecutive victory over Malawi - including three straight without conceding - making their 1-0 defeat in the sides’ first-ever meeting in a 2008 World Cup qualifier seem a distant memory.

After edging South Sudan 2-1 on the opening matchday, Malawi sat atop their AFCON qualifying group, but back-to-back defeats to Angola and, most recently, Egypt have dropped them to third, four points behind the current top two.

Without a clean sheet in five matches prior to their most recent outing, Kalisto Pasuwa’s men had well-documented defensive struggles, although few would have expected them to concede five goals in a game for the first time since losing 5-0 to Cote d’Ivoire in March 2009.

Now on a run of consecutive defeats, the Flames will look to avoid losing three games in a row for the first time in two years, as a defeat in Lilongwe would leave them hoping Angola fail to secure maximum points from their trip to Juba.

Knowing that a win definitely keeps them in the conversation for another round of matches at least, Malawi need no further incentive to target a victory against Egypt. Their attacking department, which has blanked in six of the last 10 matches, cannot afford another off day.

Back on home turf - where they have won both of their last two AFCON qualifiers by a combined score of 5-1 - Tuesday’s hosts will need their supporters in full voice as they attempt to pull off one of the biggest upsets in their history.

Malawi Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Malawi form (all competitions):.

Egypt Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Mohamed Salah’s brace last Friday moved him past Hossam Hassan to the top of Egypt’s all-time scoring charts, and the Liverpool star will be eager to extend his record.

Salah also earned his 123rd international cap in that match, moving him level with Hany Ramzy for sixth place on the all-time appearances list.

No player has scored more goals in the ongoing AFCON qualifiers than Omar Marmoush's three, making the Tottenham forward one to watch.

Richard Mbulu and Babatunde Adepoju were both substituted during Malawi’s heavy defeat in Cairo, and it would be no surprise to see either drop to the bench on Tuesday.

Should Pasuwa opt for changes in attack, Festus Duwe and Mwisho Mhango would be the most likely beneficiaries.

Malawi possible starting lineup:.

Chokooka; Nyirenda, Nyasulu, Mpokera, Chirwa; Mpinganjira, Petro, Njaliwa, Mwaungulu; Mhango, Adepoju.

Egypt possible starting lineup:.

Shobeir; Hany, Rabia, Abdelmaguid, Abdoul-Fetouh; Zizo, Lasheen, Maher; Salah, Marmoush, Trezeguet.

Egypt boast a vastly superior squad on paper, and Malawi will need the visitors to be well below their best to have any chance of an upset.

With Salah and Marmoush both in form, we expect Egypt to cruise to a routine win and book their place at the 2027 AFCON finals.

Ronaldinho spoke about his time at AC Milan and the winner scored against Inter in the derby, seeing as he’s preparing for a professional comeback in another derby.

Ronaldinho is about to make a spectacular comeback at the age of 46, set to start for the Serie C side Ravenna against Forli tomorrow. Besides being an investor in the club, the main motivation for the comeback appears to be to score his 300th career goal (currently at 299).

In a recent development, whether he will play more than just this one game remains to be seen, but the Ravenna fans are in for a special evening at their stadium. Especially since it’s a derby as well, which the Brazilian star has some experience with already in Italy.

Sources indicate that when interviewed by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, the journalist was keen to point out that Ronaldinho scored his first goal in Italy in a derby. More specifically for Milan against Inter, leading the Rossoneri to a 1-0 win in 2008.

You scored your first goal in Italy in the Milan derby….

Industry observers note that “Oh, sure, that goal against Inter while wearing the AC Milan shirt. It was my first goal in Italy, it was special, and I’ll certainly never forget it, especially because every time I return to Italy I’m practically always reminded of it.

“My time with AC Milan was wonderful, for everyone, for the people who greeted me, the goals, the memories. Now I want to make the people of Ravenna happy for their passion.”.

According to recent reports, “So many, so many. The goals, the training sessions, Milanello, that goal in the derby, my teammates, the victories. AC Milan is always a wonderful memory, no matter how you look at it.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Ukraine welcome Georgia to Kosicka futbalova arena on Tuesday night for a matchday six clash in UEFA Nations League B Group 2.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ellis Stevens | 15 Nov 2026 16:54.

Ukraine welcome Georgia to Kosicka futbalova arena on Tuesday night for a matchday six clash in UEFA Nations League B Group 2.

The hosts are third in the standings and two points ahead of their bottom-placed visitors, leaving both teams fighting to confirm their survival in League B.

Ukraine got their 2026-27 Nations League campaign underway with an encouraging 1-0 victory over Hungary, with Danylo Sikan scoring the only goal just before half-time.

After following that result up with a 0-0 draw against Georgia, Ukraine have subsequently fallen to three consecutive defeats, losing 3-0 and 1-0 to Northern Ireland and 2-1 to Hungary.

Andrea Maldera's side, as a result, sit third in Nations League B Group 2 with four points from five matches, and with just one game remaining, Ukraine are unable to climb into the promotion playoff places.

However, Ukraine are still fighting to ensure their survival in League B, as they lead visitors Georgia by only two points, meaning defeat on Tuesday would consign Maldera's men to a relegation playoff fixture.

Ukraine will secure their League B status with at least a draw, and they will, therefore, be hoping to replicate or improve upon their 0-0 stalemate with Georgia in the reverse fixture.

Georgia have failed to win any of their five League B matches, recording two draws and suffering three defeats during that time.

Despite boasting the likes of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Georges Mikautadze in attack, Georgia have also failed to find the back of the net in any of their five matches, while they have conceded four times.

Georgia will be hoping to end their goalless streak when they come up against Ukraine, who have conceded more than any other team in the group (six conceded).

However, Georgia's attack has been weakened by the long-term injury to Kvaratskhelia, who scored the nation's last goal in their 2-0 victory over Bahrain in a friendly in June.

Georgia will also have to overcome a miserable record in meetings with Ukraine, having failed to defeat Tuesday's opponents in any of their 12 meetings - losing seven and drawing five.

Ukraine form (all competitions):.

Georgia form (all competitions):.

Ukraine failed to find the net for the third time in Group 2 as they lost 1-0 to Northern Ireland last time out, and Maldera may opt to make changes in attack as a result, meaning the likes of Artem Dovbyk could start.

At the opposite end, captain Mykola Matvienko could start alongside Ilya Zabarnyi, with Illia Krupskyi introduced at right-back.

Meanwhile, Georgia will be without superstar Kvaratskhelia due to a long-term injury, meaning much of the attacking responsibility will rest on Mikautadze's shoulders.

The striker should be supported by Zuriko Davitashvili, Nika Gagnidze and Giorgi Kvernadze, with Anzor Mekvabishvili and Giorgi Chakvetadze in midfield.

Ukraine possible starting lineup:.

Trubin; Krupskyi, Zabarnyi, Matvienko, Mykolenko; Andriyevskiy, Yarmoliuk, Ocheretko, Sudakov; Dovbyk, Krasnopir.

Georgia possible starting lineup:.

Mamardashvili; Kakabadze, Goglichidze, Dvali, Lochoshvili; Chakvetadze, Mekvabishvili; Kvernadze, Gagnidze, Davitashvili; Mikautadze.

Georgia have failed to score in any of their five matches and are further weakened by Kvaratskhelia's absence, and with Ukraine boasting the home advantage, we are predicting a win for the hosts.

Latest Update: Legendary commentator CLIVE TYLDESLEY on how his ITV exit has made hearts grow fonder, the rise of YouTube streamers, his lockdown money-spinner - and why he refuses to be another loud voice in the game

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:00 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • Clive Tyldesley reaches for his glasses as he rummages through the commentary charts crammed into an old filing cabinet, jokes about his fading eyesight and supposes one day he will no longer be able to identify footballers from the gantry.
  • Fortunately, we are still far from that point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:00 EST, 15 November 2026.

Clive Tyldesley reaches for his glasses as he rummages through the commentary charts crammed into an old filing cabinet, jokes about his fading eyesight and supposes one day he will no longer be able to identify footballers from the gantry.

Fortunately, we are still far from that point. At 72, Tyldesley is calling the game as accurately as ever. His eyes are perfectly good when bespectacled, his mind nimble enough to keep up with play and his soothingly familiar voice strong and authoritative with a gentle tendency towards self-deprecation.

This much was evident as Manchester United roared back to beat Roma in the Champions League and a clip of his spine-tingling commentary from the live CBS broadcast circulated on social media and found an appreciative audience in Europe.

'I don't know if there's an element of nostalgia in hearing my voice again,' says Tyldesley. 'If I'm honest, I've dodged the worst of the public's ire with everything including commentators because I haven't been around for the last few years.

Sources indicate that 'Absence has made a few hearts grow a little fonder towards me and maybe if I'd been on Sky every week for the last six years, I'd be no less unpopular than anybody else out there. So, I can't pretend it's not nice to get some engagement with an audience I used to commentate to on a regular basis, but I'm very happy where I am.'.

Tyldesley has been the lead commentator for the CBS coverage of the Champions League since 2020, converting transfer fees into US dollars and keeping his measurements imperial for a North American audience but otherwise approaching the job as he always did.

Clive Tyldesley is calling the game as accurately as ever at 72 and is 'very happy' in his role as the lead commentator of CBS coverage of the Champions League.

Tyldesley's commentary of Man United's comeback against Roma circulated on social media and received an appreciative audience in Europe.

The 72-year-old wonders whether there was an element of nostalgia to the reaction, with Tyldesley's work for CBS meaning his commentary cannot be shown in Europe.

Clips of the studio panel featuring Thierry Henry, Micah Richards, Jamie Carragher and presenter Kate Scott are popular on social media but live action featuring Tyldesley's commentary is governed by broadcasting rights deals and cannot be shown in Europe.

The one from Old Trafford of Matheus Cunha's winning goal in the 86th minute slipped through the net on X and reminded everyone his passion for football is undimmed, and his voice can still stand hairs on attention.

Recent findings suggest that 'I don't think I've seen a better game than the first leg of the Paris Saint-Germain v Bayern Munich Champions League semi-final,' says Tyldesley on the rare quality of Europe's elite competition. 'I listened to people with hundreds more England caps than me saying it was bad defending, but I watched the whole game back the next day and it wasn't.

According to recent reports, 'I'm sorry but it was wonderful attacking and a show of intent by two coaches who trusted defenders to defend one-on-one and attackers to score more than the opposition. Rob Green was my co-commentator and at the end we just put our microphones down and looked at each other and remarked, "Wow.".

'I've not forgotten muddy pitches and assassin centre backs. You only need to look on YouTube to see football was different, but you can't pretend it was better. I see terrible games today just as I did then, but particularly in the Champions League, I regularly stumble upon football that gets me off my seat.'.

His exit from ITV, first displaced by Sam Matterface as lead commentator in 2020 and then released entirely after Euro 2024 clearly smarted but Tyldesley is comfortable as the veteran in the fast-changing media landscape.

Industry observers note that 'Most of the principles I picked up from watching John Motson, Barry Davies and Brian Moore in their pomp are applicable to commentary in 2026,' he states. 'There's no need to reinvent that particular wheel.

It has been revealed that 'You can offer alternatives such as fan zones and screaming watchalongs for people to view it in a different way. I make it my business to look at J_Tekkz or LDN Movements or whatever is pulling in millions on YouTube.

Tyldesley believes he has not seen a better game than the first leg of PSG's Champions League semi-final with Bayern Munich last year.

The veteran commentator believes most of the principles he learned starting out still apply, but admits to having watched popular newly introduced voices to see if anything could apply to his commentary.

Tyldesley also works as a guest lecturer and commentates for blockbuster computer games, as well as selling framed prints of his commentary charts.

'I sample a bit of Mark Goldbridge to see why he's prominent but I'm hearing nothing in those guys applicable to the way I call a football match so I carry on with the same focus I've always had on what constitutes good commentary.'.

The central principle being that the game is bigger than the individuals in it, he points out, with viewers tuning in for the football not the commentator.

'The biggest challenge for a television commentator is to find the right words at the major moments, to go beyond "amazing," "brilliant", "incredible" and try to add some editorial context,' says Tyldesley.

In a recent development, 'Every goal is unique. The words following a goal that is going to be remembered for years should be unique and specific to that goal, but that's difficult to do. It's unscripted performance and difficult to master and capture.

'I am concentrating hardest for the 10-15 seconds after a massive goal because I'm searching for words which will become a small part of people's memories. That's very different to consciously trying to provide 45-second soundbites to amplify one's own personality and standing on social media.

'There's a danger of media leaning that way as it develops such an emphasis on the bitesize.'.

Among other things, Tyldesley is a guest lecturer for media students at the University of Salford, still doing commentaries for blockbuster computer games and selling framed prints of his commentary charts, something that started as 'a silly idea in lockdown'.

Recent findings suggest that his wife Susan bought a dozen frames to see how it went. Originally, he offered three Champions League finals won by English clubs in 1999, 2005 and 2012. He sent one each to Gary Neville who played for Manchester United in 1999 and Jamie Carragher who played for Liverpool in 2005. They both posted images online and demand skyrocketed.

'Two good friends,' smiles Tyldesley. 'I probably got about half a million pounds of free advertising out of them.' Sales have soared beyond 50,000. There's a Celtic chart on the gym in Rod Stewart's house. Ant and Dec have bought signed Newcastle charts.

His own venture into podcasting was short-lived and he politely declines between five and ten invitations each week to appear on others.

'I've tried to step back from that kind of thing,' claims Tyldesley. 'So much content I hear on football is empty, verbose and repetitive. Really, there are only so many things you can say about Alexander Isak having his shirt pulled in mid-air and Gary Neville probably noted most of them in the 30 seconds following the incident.

Tyldesley has no aims to retire and Paramount, the owners of his employers CBS - and soon to be the owners of TNT Sports - will have the UK rights for the Champions League.

Sales of his framed commentary charts, something that started during lockdown, have soared beyond 50,000.

'There are so many brutally judgmental loud voices in and around football attracting attention that I want to be as far away from as possible, so that's what I do. Unless I sense an opportunity to talk about communication and broadcasting rather than whether club A, B or C should replace their manager. That's not for me Clive.'.

In a recent development, so, there's a little less Tyldesley out there than there was. He was content to stay at home and watch the World Cup from his sofa this summer for the first time since 1990.

But there are no aims to retire. And who knows what might change next season when Paramount, the owners of CBS – and soon to be the owners of current rights holders TNT Sports – have the UK rights for the Champions League.

There might be a familiar voice beamed into our living rooms once again.

When I saw the Dear England play, I was the only person in the theatre who didn't enjoy it, and that was because I hated the portrayal of Harry Kane.

Sources indicate that he was written as an uneducated numbskull. Written to laugh at and the theatre laughed at him. He was stupid and gullible, another thick footballer.

And anyone who has spent time with footballers will know they might lack for an Eton College education but are streetwise and invariably smart with a razor sharp sense of humour.

Kane is a leader of those men. There's not a single thing about the person Kane has made himself to laugh or sneer at and I wanted to stand up in the theatre that afternoon and shout at everyone.

Oddly, I was introduced to the playwright James Graham at a function a few weeks later and he kind of pushed me for my opinion of Dear England.

I tried to be diplomatic, but I felt so strongly I ended up scolding him for writing a character called Harry Kane who was nothing like Harry Kane.

So, that was the end of a beautiful friendship before it began. And I'm so thrilled now there's a better appreciation of the person Harry is.

Saka heads Madueke’s left-wing cross on to the roof of the net when trying to direct it back into the middle.

Arsenal fans must be thinking this is a job for the box-crasher himself, Mikel Merino.

Leeds squeeze Arsenal’s attack again and the ball runs out for a goalkick after Odegaard’s attempt to free White down the right fails.

No changes. Tanaka needs to be more discreet this half if he is to avoid a second yellow card. Arsenal attack swiftly down the right buy Muharemovic sticks with Saka all the way to usher the ball out for a goalkick.

8 - Arsenal (5) and Leeds United (3) recorded eight offsides in total in the first half, the most in the opening 45 minutes of a Premier League game since Manchester United v Aston Villa in April 2023 (also 8). Lines. https://t.co/er4wTVAIJS.

Justin sweeps up for Leeds when Arsenal try to play head tennis on the Leeds box. Moments before Saka had ended up horizontally in the box when Muharemovic was shielding a long ball back to Trafford. The home crowd wants a penalty but no way.

According to recent reports, ally McCoist is ladling praise on Leeds’ organisation and discipline. And has special garlands for Calvert-Lewin who feels the referee is giving him nothing when manhandled by Konsa and Gabriel.

Great save from Raya when Gudmundsson’s thumping volley on the end of Bogle’s superb, deep cross is blocked at the near post. Okafor set the move going with a fine crossfield pass.

Two more Leeds names in the book: Ampadu for a late foul on Odegaard and Farke’s when the fourth official dobs him in to referee for something he said.

The crowd is growing frustrated by how well Leeds are playing and how little space they are allowing Arsenal.

Tanaka loses the ball in midfield and Arsenal pile forward but Leeds mass the ranks of their defence and block the path to goal until Justin is fouled to relieve the siege.

Leeds’ offside trap has been functioning well and now Arsenal’s well-oiled one kicks in to catch Gudmundsson and Okafor.

Arsenal in red and white, Leeds in yellow and black. Long international break, we recovered most of our players and have a point to prove after our last game.

Everyone is fit and ready to play but we have a very difficult opponent.

But we didn’t win our good start in the lottery we earned it. We travel here in confidence.

Brighton didn’t park the bus. They went for it and pressed Arsenal. You need to do this. You have to go for it. If you sit deep their individual quality is too good. The one thing is to have a proposal and a theory but another to execute it.

Last season we faced one of the best sides in the world so we didn’t dwell on [those defeats]. If we are at our best we have a chance to compete for points.

Industry observers note that right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

According to recent reports, arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Divock Origi has discussed what went wrong during his time at AC Milan, from the injuries to the Rossoneri’s decision to exclude him.

Origi joined Milan after the Scudetto season, i.e. the summer of 2022, and the idea was that he would be able to alternate with Olivier Giroud. However, a couple of injuries made his start difficult and it only went downhill from there.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Despite making 36 appearances in his first season, he got just two goals and was thus sent out on loan for the next season, joining Nottingham Forest. One goal and one assist later, he returned to Milan, where it was promptly decided that he was no longer part of the project.

Sources indicate that instead of taking the opportunity to continue his career elsewhere, Origi decided to stay and train on his own. His hefty salary of €4m net (€5.24m gross) frustrated Milan and in December 2025, they finally got the striker to terminate his contract six months earlier than its expiration.

In short, it was a costly deal for Milan and for Origi, the move effectively killed his career. Speaking to the Belgian outlet HLN.be, as cited by MilanPress, the former striker explained what happened and why he then decided to retire (in the summer of 2026).

It has been revealed that “At 27, my time at Liverpool was over. Sometimes you need to step out of your comfort zone and take on a new challenge. It’s the only way to grow as a person. AC Milan was a very interesting project.

“Paolo Maldini signed me and I felt he truly believed in me. It’s just that I got injured. Usually, I work on my preparation with my personal trainer, but this time it didn’t work. I lost much of my basic fitness; it was difficult.”.

“I don’t take it personally. It was a professional decision. Was I happy about it? Obviously not. But can I understand it? Yes. I was left out of the squad for a while and wasn’t allowed to train with the first team.

“There was the option of joining the youth team. I can’t say too much about some things for contractual reasons… Let’s just say we weren’t on the same page about it. My experience helped me keep a clear head.

“I was convinced that if you have the right intentions, everything will work out for the best in the end.”.

According to recent reports, “I had options in football, but for me it was also a time when I was starting to think about my future away from the sport. Don’t get me wrong, I’ve always dedicated myself body and soul to football. It was my great passion, ” he stated.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 15 Nov 2026 18:34, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 18:46.
  • England and Spain have confirmed their starting lineups for Sunday's UEFA Nations League showdown at the Metropolitano Stadium.
  • Thomas Tuchel's men must beat the world and European champions to win League A Group 3, although both sides have already sealed their spots in the quarter-finals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 15 Nov 2026 18:34, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 18:46.

England and Spain have confirmed their starting lineups for Sunday's UEFA Nations League showdown at the Metropolitano Stadium.

Thomas Tuchel's men must beat the world and European champions to win League A Group 3, although both sides have already sealed their spots in the quarter-finals.

The Three Lions have made three changes for their reunion with La Roja, all of which come in defence, including the already-known switch in goal between James Trafford and Jordan Pickford.

Tuchel has also brought Ben White - who was once again booed by England fans against Croatia on Thursday - back into the starting XI, at the expense of Trent Alexander-Arnold.

Fellow Arsenal man Ezri Konsa is also restored to the starting lineup after missing the midweek victory through injury, taking Dan Burn's place in the heart of defence.

Djed Spence and Myles Lewis-Skelly must make do with spots on the bench following their returns from injury and suspension respectively, as Tuchel sticks with an unchanged midfield and attacking selection.

As for Spain, head coach Luis de la Fuente has made five changes to the side that bested the Czech Republic 2-0 last time out, including expected recalls for Lamine Yamal and Mikel Oyarzabal.

The pair both missed Spain's penultimate group game as a precautionary measure, but they have unsurprisingly been selected over Yeremy Pino and Ferran Torres this time around.

De la Fuente has also made a bold call in the number 10 role, demoting Fermin Lopez in favour of Mikel Merino, but Alex Baena hold his spot on the left over Nico Williams - now fully fit again following illness.

Merino's Arsenal teammate Martin Zubimendi is also retained in midfield over Pedri, despite concerns over fatigue having played the full 90 against the Czech Republic amid a lack of game time at club level.

De la Fuente has made two changes to his backline foe the final matchday, as Marc Pubill replaces Pedro Porro at right-back, and Aymeric Laporte is in for Dean Huijsen in central defence.

England XI: Trafford; White, Konsa, Quansah, Hall; Anderson, Rice; Rogers, Ju. Bellingham, Gordon; Kane.

It has been revealed that subs: Pickford, Alexander-Arnold, Steele, Gibbs-White, Spence, Burn, Jo. Bellingham, Hill, Calvert-Lewin, Ngumoha, Eze, Lewis-Skelly.

Spain XI: Simon; Pubill, Cubarsi, Laporte, Cucurella; Zubimendi, Ruiz; Yamal, Merino, Baena; Oyarzabal.

Subs: Raya, Garcia, Roca, Huijsen, Torres. Lopez, Pino, Porro, Barrios, Munoz, Williams, Pedri.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joel Lefevre | 15 Nov 2026 19:06.
  • On Tuesday, the USA aim to give their manager a fitting send-off when they host Haiti in the second leg of that quarter-final CONCACAF Nations League tie at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati.
  • It would require an epic collapse for the Yanks to be eliminated from this tournament on Tuesday, having beaten the Haitians 6-0 in leg one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 15 Nov 2026 19:06.

On Tuesday, the USA aim to give their manager a fitting send-off when they host Haiti in the second leg of that quarter-final CONCACAF Nations League tie at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati.

It would require an epic collapse for the Yanks to be eliminated from this tournament on Tuesday, having beaten the Haitians 6-0 in leg one.

For the final time, Mauricio Pochettino will be on the US sidelines Tuesday, hoping to end his tenure on a positive note before heading to Old Trafford to join Manchester United.

While he leaves the national team program without a trophy, the Argentine coach has seen this team flourish since the World Cup concluded, and they are currently on a five-match winning run across all competitions.

Pochettino’s men have been near-flawless since the fall, posting three successive clean sheets while netting three or more goals in four of their last five encounters.

The US have only lost three Nations League knockout matches, boasting a 100% home record in quarter-final outings.

Tuesday will mark their fifth international at TQL Stadium, with the Yanks undefeated at the venue, including two wins.

They are unbeaten in their last 11 internationals against Haiti, winning those last four meetings by a combined margin of 10-1.

David Badia’s men have lost their last two matches by a combined margin of 8-0 after winning their first three Nations League group outings.

The Haitians have not won a quarter-final contest in a CONCACAF competition since the 2019 Gold Cup when they were down 2-0 and stunned Canada 3-2.

They have not lost a League A encounter in this tournament when netting the opening goal since the 2023 group stage when Jamaica beat them 3-2.

Les Grenadiers can claim their first victory over the US on American soil Tuesday since 1969, when they beat them 1-0 in a World Cup qualifier in San Diego.

USA CONCACAF Nations League form:.

Haiti CONCACAF Nations League form:.

At 18, Julian Hall was the youngest player in the US starting 11 on Saturday, while Santiago Casteneda and Reed Baker-Whiting are seeking their first senior caps.

Christian Pulisic and Weston McKennie both featured for the first time since the World Cup this past weekend, with the former netting a brace and the latter adding one, with Hall, Auston Trusty and Folarin Balogun also scoring.

There are two Haitian players without a cap to their name, including goalkeeper Jonah Mednard and midfielder Miguel Joseph.

Fabrice Picault will hope to draw into the starting 11, as he, Ruben Providence and Yassin Fortune were among those who began on the bench for them on Saturday.

Freese; Freeman, McKenzie, Trusty, A. Robinson; McGlynn, Adams; Sullivan, Ellis, Albert; Balogun.

Haiti possible starting lineup:.

A. Pierre; Arcus, K. Pierre, Delcroix, Experience; L. Pierre, Jean Jacques; Picault, Casimir, Isidor Fortune.

The Americans have been miles ahead of their CONCACAF opponents since the World Cup concluded, and even if the squad is heavily rotated, we trust they will emerge with another comfortable victory and send Pochettino off in style.

  • Manchester United are reportedly showing interest in Fulham defender Calvin Bassey ahead of the January transfer window.
  • The Red Devils are languishing in 18th place in the Premier League table, and Mauricio Pochettino has a huge task on his hands to pull the club out of their current predicament.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 15 Nov 2026 19:32.

Manchester United are reportedly showing interest in Fulham defender Calvin Bassey ahead of the January transfer window.

The Red Devils are languishing in 18th place in the Premier League table, and Mauricio Pochettino has a huge task on his hands to pull the club out of their current predicament.

While his primary objective will be to steer United away from the relegation zone, the club must swiftly turn their attention to the winter transfer window, with strengthening the defence an urgent priority.

According to The Telegraph, Bassey has emerged as a strong option for Man Utd after impressing for Fulham over the past few years.

Bassey joined Fulham in the summer of 2023 after spending a season at Ajax, having previously enjoyed a two-year spell with Glasgow Rangers.

The Nigerian defender has made more than 110 appearances for the Cottagers across all competitions, scoring four goals.

The 26-year-old has featured nine times in the Premier League this season, and his experience could prove valuable to Man Utd, who have already conceded 19 goals in 10 matches.

Bassey offers considerable physical presence and pace at the back, two qualities that the Red Devils have arguably lacked this season.

Furthermore, the former Gers defender can also operate at left-back, which would provide Pochettino with another option given Luke Shaw's injury record.

It would be difficult for Bassey to dismiss an offer from Man Utd outright, regardless of their current position in the league.

The defender's contract at Craven Cottage runs until next summer, although Fulham have the option to extend it by a further 12 months.

Arvada Arbeloa regards Bassey as one of the best defenders in the Premier League, but whether Fulham can hold on to him if the Red Devils table a tempting offer remains a major question.

#14488. Engineered bacteria are weaning farms away from synthetic fertilizers

Engineered bacteria are weaning farms away from synthetic fertilizers

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that scientists are engineering bacteria that can provide nitrogen, an essential ingredient for plant growth, to wheat crops.
  • In a recent development, the world’s farms depend on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers to increase crop yields, but the production and use of these chemicals generates billions of tonnes of greenhouse-gas emissions every year.
  • This approach takes a cue from natural bacteria that ‘fix’ nitrogen into a useful form and provide it to certain plants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that scientists are engineering bacteria that can provide nitrogen, an essential ingredient for plant growth, to wheat crops. Credit: Shakeel Ahmed/Anadolu Agency/Getty.

In a recent development, the world’s farms depend on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers to increase crop yields, but the production and use of these chemicals generates billions of tonnes of greenhouse-gas emissions every year. Now, scientists are making progress on a greener alternative: bioengineered bacteria.

This approach takes a cue from natural bacteria that ‘fix’ nitrogen into a useful form and provide it to certain plants. Scientists are engineering genetic features into bacteria with the aim of enabling them to fix nitrogen for important food crops, such as maize (corn) and wheat, that don’t have such natural microbial partners.

In a comment published on 10 November in Nature Biotechnology1, researchers suggest that bioengineered bacteria could eventually replace up to half of synthetic fertilizers. The bacteria deliver nitrogen more efficiently to roots than synthetic fertilizers do, which could reduce greenhouse-gas emissions and nitrogen pollution of waterways. But this would require a slew of advances, from getting different microbial species to work together to more-rigorous field trials.

Recent findings suggest that how CRISPR could yield the next blockbuster cropSome of these ‘biofertilizers’ have been augmented with genes and genetic snippets from viruses or distantly related bacteria. This means that the engineered microbes are classified as transgenic — altered to include DNA from other species. The bacteria are now being trialled on small plots of maize on farms in the Midwestern United States. The bacteria, developed by Switch Bioworks in San Carlos, California, are the first example of a transgenic biofertilizer approved for testing on fields in the country.

How CRISPR could yield the next blockbuster crop.

In September, Switch Bioworks received approval from the Brazilian regulatory agency, the National Technical Commission on Biosafety (CNTBio), to test its strains there. This is the first time that a transgenic bacterium of any kind has been approved for field tests in Brazil, claims molecular biologist Mario Murakami, who is the president of CTNBio in Campinas.

It has been revealed that companies that have focused on editing bacterial genes rather than producing transgenic microbes are further along. Pivot Bio in Minneapolis, Minnesota, has applied its gene-edited biofertilizers to tens of millions of hectares of US farmland over the past decade, notes the organization’s chief technology officer Travis Frey. Some of Pivot Bio’s products have also been tested in Canada, Argentina, Kenya and Brazil.

Sources indicate that most plants can’t use the form of nitrogen that is present in the air. Some crops, including soya beans and peanuts, host colonies of bacteria that can convert atmospheric nitrogen into a usable form. The plant takes up that nitrogen and, in return, provides carbon that fuels bacterial growth. But most staple crops lack these microbial partners, leading farmers to rely on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers. These chemical fertilizers account for 5% of global greenhouse-gas emissions, and drive damaging nutrient pollution in waterways.

For decades, researchers have tried to get bacteria to fix nitrogen for staple crops. Until recently, the approach was to collect wild strains of nitrogen-fixing bacteria from soil and apply them to seeds or spray them onto plants. “It doesn’t work,” notes Jean-Michel Ané, a bioengineer at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, who is working on microbial fertilizers. The wild microbes fail to thrive when applied to crops that don’t provide them with carbon.

How to climate-proof crops: scientists say the secret’s in the dirt.
